Recognize that under these conditions, a group of atoms can occupy the same quantum state.
Identify that this phenomenon leads to the formation of a new state of matter.
Conclude that this state of matter is known as Bose-Einstein condensate.

text: Which of the following is forbidden by the Pauli exclusion principle?
choices: Neutrons in a nucleus out-numbering the protons
Triple ionization of the lanthanide [LAN-thuh-nyd] series
The sharing of more than one electron by any two atoms
Two electrons in the exact same state in an atomic shell
explainAnswer: Understand the Pauli exclusion principle, which states that no two fermions (like electrons) can occupy the same quantum state simultaneously.
Evaluate each choice to see if it involves two identical fermions in the same state.
Identify that 'two electrons in the exact same state in an atomic shell' directly violates this principle.
Conclude that this option is forbidden by the Pauli exclusion principle.

text: What is the term for a chemical half-reaction that results in a gain of electrons?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of half-reactions in redox chemistry.
Understand that a half-reaction involves either the gain or loss of electrons.
Recognize that gaining electrons corresponds to a decrease in oxidation state.
Define the term associated with gaining electrons as reduction.

text: Using proper chemical nomenclature and indicating the state of each substance as solid, liquid, aqueous [AY-kwee-uhs], or gas, what is a balanced equation for the reaction in which silver nitrate solution is mixed with sodium chloride solution, producing insoluble silver chloride and sodium nitrate solution?
explainAnswer: Identify the reactants: silver nitrate (AgNO3, aqueous) and sodium chloride (NaCl, aqueous).
Write the products of the reaction: silver chloride (AgCl, solid) and sodium nitrate (NaNO3, aqueous).
Write the unbalanced equation: AgNO3(aq) + NaCl(aq) -> AgCl(s) + NaNO3(aq).
Balance the equation by ensuring the number of each type of atom is equal on both sides.
Confirm the states of each substance are correctly indicated.

text: Identify all of the following three substances that are more acidic than distilled water: 1) Lemon juice; 2) Milk; 3) Ammonia.
explainAnswer: Understand that acidity is measured by pH, with lower pH values indicating higher acidity.
Know that distilled water has a neutral pH of 7.
Research or recall the pH values of lemon juice (approximately 2-3), milk (approximately 6-7), and ammonia (approximately 11).
Compare the pH values of each substance to that of distilled water to determine which are more acidic.

text: Identify all of the following four processes that are endothermic reactions: 1) exploding dynamite, 2) burning wood, 3) baking bread, 4) melting ice cubes.
explainAnswer: Understand that endothermic reactions absorb heat from their surroundings.
Identify the processes listed and determine if they absorb heat or release heat.
Recognize that baking bread requires heat to cause chemical changes, making it endothermic.
Note that melting ice cubes also absorbs heat to change from solid to liquid, classifying it as endothermic.
Conclude that the correct endothermic processes are baking bread and melting ice cubes.

text: How many neutrons does a single atom of carbon-13 possess?
explainAnswer: Identify the atomic number of carbon, which is 6.
Understand that the atomic mass of carbon-13 is 13.
Subtract the atomic number from the atomic mass to find the number of neutrons: 13 - 6.
Calculate the result, which is 7 neutrons.

text: Light typically travels in waves that are oriented in all planes traveling in a given direction. What is the term for light waves that are traveling in one plane?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of light waves and their behavior.
Understand the concept of orientation in wave motion.
Recognize that light waves can be restricted to a single plane.
Define the term used to describe light waves that are oriented in one plane.

text: Using proper chemical nomenclature, indicating the charge of each ion, what is the balanced net ionic equation for the reaction between barium chloride and potassium phosphate?
explainAnswer: Identify the reactants and their ionic forms: Barium chloride (BaCl2) dissociates into Ba^2+ and 2Cl^- ions, and potassium phosphate (K3PO4) dissociates into 3K^+ and PO4^3- ions.
Write the complete ionic equation by combining the ions from both reactants: 3Ba^2+ + 6Cl^- + 3K^+ + PO4^3-.
Identify and remove the spectator ions, which do not participate in the reaction; in this case, Cl^- and K^+ are spectator ions.
Write the net ionic equation using the remaining ions: 3Ba^2+ + PO4^3- → Ba3(PO4)2.
Ensure the equation is balanced in terms of both charge and mass.

text: What group of elements have a shiny luster and are good conductors of heat and electricity?
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of elements that are shiny and conduct heat and electricity well.
Recall the classification of elements in the periodic table.
Determine which category of elements exhibits these properties.
Conclude that the group of elements that are shiny and good conductors is metals.

text: Which of the following molecules is considered the most polar:
explainAnswer: Identify the electronegativity values of the atoms in each molecule.
Determine the difference in electronegativity between the bonded atoms to assess polarity.
Consider the molecular geometry to see if the dipoles cancel out or not.
Compare the overall polarity of each molecule based on the previous analyses.

text: What volume, in milliliters, of a 10 molar hydrochloric acid stock solution is needed to make 2 liters of a 3 molar hydrochloric acid solution?
explainAnswer: Convert the desired final volume from liters to milliliters by multiplying by 1000, which gives 2000 mL.

Use the dilution equation, which states that C1V1 = C2V2, where C1 is the concentration of the stock solution, V1 is the volume of the stock solution needed, C2 is the concentration of the diluted solution, and V2 is the volume of the diluted solution.
Substitute the known values into the equation: 10 mol/L * V1 = 3 mol/L * 2000 mL.
Solve for V1 by rearranging the equation: V1 = (3 mol/L * 2000 mL) / 10 mol/L.
Calculate V1 to find that it equals 600 mL.

text: Which of the following best explains why Erlenmeyer flasks are good for mixing samples?
choices: Magnetic stirrers can easily enter and exit the mouth
They have straight sides that allow for complete mixing
They have slanted sides that prevent spilling and don't require additional stirring equipment
Their narrow necks make pouring and transferring spill resistant
explainAnswer: Identify the key features of Erlenmeyer flasks.
Evaluate each choice based on how well it describes the advantages of Erlenmeyer flasks.
Focus on the design elements that contribute to mixing and spill prevention.
Select the option that best summarizes the benefits of the flask's shape and functionality.

text: In a reaction that runs to completion, 3 moles of substance A react with 5 moles of substance B to create 2 moles of substance C. To create 18 moles of substance C, what is the total number of moles of reactants required?
explainAnswer: Identify the mole ratio of reactants A and B to product C from the reaction, which is 3 moles of A and 5 moles of B for every 2 moles of C.
Determine how many times the reaction must occur to produce 18 moles of C by dividing 18 by 2, which equals 9.
Calculate the total moles of A needed by multiplying 3 moles of A by 9, resulting in 27 moles of A.
Calculate the total moles of B needed by multiplying 5 moles of B by 9, resulting in 45 moles of B.
Add the total moles of A and B together: 27 moles of A + 45 moles of B equals 72 moles of reactants.

text: In a given reaction, three moles of Substance A react completely with two moles of Substance B to create Substances C and D. The reaction continues to completion and feels cold to the touch, but neither Substance A nor B was cold to the touch prior to the reaction. Which of the following is TRUE regarding the reaction?
choices: There was a total of 5 moles of products created
Substance B is the limiting reagent
The activation energy of the reaction is less than the activation energy of the reverse reaction
explainAnswer: Identify the reactants and their mole ratios from the reaction.
Determine which reactant is present in a smaller amount relative to the stoichiometric ratios required for the reaction.
Since three moles of Substance A react with two moles of Substance B, compare the available moles of each reactant.
Conclude that if Substance B is present in a smaller amount than required, it is the limiting reagent.

text: What graduated piece of glassware is used for delivering known volume of a liquid, especially during titrations?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which involves laboratory equipment used in chemistry.
Recall the common types of glassware used for measuring and delivering liquids.
Consider the specific function of each type of glassware, focusing on those used for precise volume delivery.
Determine which piece of glassware is specifically designed for titrations and allows for controlled dispensing of liquid.
Conclude that the correct answer is the burette, as it is used for delivering known volumes of liquid in titrations.

text: If the air in a room is in a gaseous state of matter, what happens to the molecules that make up the gas when the temperature in the room increases?
answer: THEY MOVE FASTER (ACCEPT: MOLECULES MOVE FURTHER APART,
explainAnswer: Understand that gas molecules are in constant motion.
Recognize that temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the molecules.
Realize that an increase in temperature means an increase in kinetic energy.
Conclude that as the kinetic energy increases, the molecules move faster and may also move further apart.

text: Which of the following elements is often added to steel to make it harder?
explainAnswer: Identify the purpose of adding elements to steel, which is to enhance its properties.
Review the properties of each element listed in the choices.
Determine which element is known for increasing hardness and strength in steel.
Select the element that is commonly used in steel alloys for this purpose, which is chromium.

text: What two natural amino acids contain sulfur?
explainAnswer: Recall the basic structure of amino acids and their common elements.
Identify the amino acids that are known to contain sulfur in their side chains.
List the amino acids that contain sulfur, which are cysteine and methionine.
Confirm that these are the only two natural amino acids containing sulfur.

text: Which of the following elements is found in Period 2 and Group 4A of the Periodic Table:
explainAnswer: Identify the elements listed in the choices: sulfur, carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen.
Locate Period 2 in the Periodic Table and identify the elements present in that period.
Determine which of the elements in Period 2 belongs to Group 4A (or Group 14).
Confirm that carbon is the only element from the choices that is in Period 2 and Group 4A.

text: For a graph of a sinusoidal [sy-nuh-SOID-l] sound wave function, which of the following quantities can be on the x axis?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of a sinusoidal wave function.
Determine the typical variables represented on the x-axis in wave graphs.
Evaluate each choice to see if it can logically represent a position on the x-axis.
Conclude that 'Position' is the only quantity that can be on the x-axis for a sinusoidal sound wave.

text: Astronomers and physicists believe that the universe's expansion is accelerating due to the action of what undiscovered form of energy that composes 73% of the universe’s mass-energy?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in the question, such as 'universe's expansion', 'accelerating', and 'undiscovered form of energy'.
Recall that the majority of the universe's mass-energy is attributed to something that is not directly observable.
Consider the current theories in cosmology regarding the components of the universe, particularly those that account for its expansion.
Recognize that the term commonly used to describe this mysterious energy is 'dark energy'.
Conclude that the answer to the question is 'dark energy' based on the understanding of its role in the universe.

text: Which of the following atoms has the largest atomic radius?
explainAnswer: Identify the trend of atomic radius in the periodic table, which increases down a group and decreases across a period.
Locate each element on the periodic table: Potassium (K) is in Group 1, Carbon (C) in Group 14, Hydrogen (H) in Group 1, and Fluorine (F) in Group 17.
Note that Potassium is further down in Group 1 compared to Hydrogen, which means it has a larger atomic radius due to additional electron shells.
Compare the positions of Carbon and Fluorine, which are both in higher periods and have smaller radii than Potassium.
Conclude that Potassium has the largest atomic radius among the given choices.

text: Transition metals are characterized as elements with partially-filled configurations of what electron subshell?
explainAnswer: Identify the electron subshells relevant to transition metals, which are typically found in the d-block of the periodic table.
Recall that transition metals have partially-filled d subshells, which distinguishes them from other elements.
Understand that the presence of unpaired electrons in the d subshell contributes to the unique properties of transition metals.
Conclude that the correct answer is the d subshell, as it is the one that is partially filled in transition metals.

text: How many moles of hydrogen gas may be obtained from one mole of water?
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical formula for water, which is H2O.
Determine the number of hydrogen atoms in one molecule of water, which is 2.
Recognize that 1 mole of water contains 2 moles of hydrogen atoms.
Since the question asks for moles of hydrogen gas (H2), divide the number of moles of hydrogen atoms by 2.
Conclude that 1 mole of water produces 1 mole of hydrogen gas.

text: Organic chemistry is a field of chemistry primarily devoted to studying compounds containing what element?
explainAnswer: Identify the focus of organic chemistry, which is the study of compounds.
Recall that organic compounds are primarily defined by the presence of specific elements.
Recognize that carbon is the key element that characterizes organic compounds.
Conclude that the element primarily studied in organic chemistry is carbon.

text: What is the term for the minimum amount of energy required to remove an electron from an atom in the gaseous phase?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept related to the removal of an electron from an atom.
Recall that this process occurs in the gaseous phase.
Understand that the energy required for this process is a specific term in chemistry.
Conclude that the term for this minimum energy is ionization energy.

text: How many grams of potassium chloride, with a molecular weight of 104, must be dissolved in 250 milliliters of water to make a 20% potassium chloride solution?
explainAnswer: Determine the total mass of the solution needed for a 20% concentration by using the formula: mass of solute = concentration × total mass of solution.
Since the solution is 250 mL of water and the density of water is approximately 1 g/mL, the total mass of the solution is about 250 grams.
Calculate the mass of potassium chloride needed by multiplying the total mass of the solution (250 grams) by the percentage concentration (20%).
Convert the percentage to a decimal (0.20) and multiply: 250 grams × 0.20 = 50 grams.
Thus, you need to dissolve 50 grams of potassium chloride in 250 mL of water.

text: Which of the following is a diatomic molecule?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of a diatomic molecule, which consists of two atoms of the same or different elements.
Examine each choice to determine if it consists of two atoms.
Recognize that H2 is made up of two hydrogen atoms, making it a diatomic molecule.
Confirm that the other options (H2O, methane, and NaCl) consist of more than two atoms or different types of atoms.

text: What is the term for the tendency of an object to resist changes in its motion?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept related to motion and forces in physics.
Recall the definition of inertia as it relates to an object's resistance to changes in its state of motion.
Recognize that inertia is a fundamental property of matter.
Conclude that the term you are looking for is inertia.

text: Amy is pulling a heavy cart. It is harder to start pulling the cart than to keep the cart in motion, because kinetic friction:
choices: Is zero once the cart is moving
Is only present when the cart is first pulled
explainAnswer: Understand that static friction acts on an object at rest and must be overcome to start its motion.
Recognize that once the object is in motion, kinetic friction takes over, which is generally lower than static friction.
Identify that the question is asking about the difference between static and kinetic friction.
Conclude that since it is harder to start pulling the cart, it indicates that static friction is greater than kinetic friction.

text: Which of the following metals has the most similar valence electron configuration to silver?
explainAnswer: Identify the valence electron configuration of silver, which is [Kr] 4d10 5s1.
Examine the valence electron configurations of the given choices: Iridium ([Xe] 4f14 5d7 6s2), Rhodium ([Kr] 4d8 5s2), Titanium ([Ar] 3d2 4s2), and Gold ([Xe] 4f14 5d10 6s1).
Compare the valence electron configurations to find the one that closely matches silver's configuration.
Determine that Gold has a similar configuration with 5d10 6s1, making it the correct answer.

text: It takes 6 joules of energy to stretch a Hookean spring from its equilibrium position to a displacement of 40 centimeters. How many additional joules of energy will it require to stretch it from 40 centimeters to 80 centimeters away from equilibrium?
explainAnswer: Recognize that the energy stored in a Hookean spring is given by the formula E = 1/2 k x^2, where E is energy, k is the spring constant, and x is the displacement from equilibrium.
Use the information that it takes 6 joules to stretch the spring to 40 centimeters (0.4 meters) to set up the equation: 6 = 1/2 k (0.4)^2.
Solve for the spring constant k using the equation: k = 6 / (1/2 * (0.4)^2).
Calculate the energy required to stretch the spring to 80 centimeters (0.8 meters) using the formula: E = 1/2 k (0.8)^2.
Subtract the energy already used (6 joules) from the total energy calculated for 80 centimeters to find the additional energy required.

text: In nuclear reactors, control rods are used to absorb free neutrons without undergoing fission themselves. Which of the following is a frequently used substance to make control rods?
explainAnswer: Identify the purpose of control rods in nuclear reactors, which is to absorb free neutrons.
Review the properties of the given substances to determine which can effectively absorb neutrons.
Recognize that boron is known for its neutron-absorbing capabilities.
Eliminate the other options (Carbon, Iron, Water) based on their lesser effectiveness in neutron absorption compared to boron.

text: Which of the following is true about a mixture of gasses?
choices: The sum of the partial pressures of each gas is equal to the total pressure
The sum of the temperatures of each gas is equal to the total temperature
The total volume is equal to the largest partial volume
The total number of moles is equal to the total volume multiplied by the sum of the moles of each gas
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of partial pressure in a mixture of gases, which states that each gas in a mixture exerts pressure independently.
Recall Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures, which states that the total pressure of a gas mixture is the sum of the partial pressures of each individual gas.
Evaluate the other choices to see if they align with gas laws and principles.
Conclude that the correct answer is the one that accurately reflects Dalton's Law.

text: An ice cube dyed with red food coloring is placed into a cup of fresh water at room temperature. An identical cube is placed into salt water. Where will the color go as the ice cubes melt?
choices: Bottom of the cup in fresh water and top of the cup in salt water
Top of the cup in fresh water and bottom of the cup in salt water
Mixed into the water in both cups
Bottom of the cup in both cups
explainAnswer: Understand that the density of fresh water is less than that of salt water.
Recognize that as the ice melts in fresh water, the dye will sink to the bottom due to the density of the colored water being higher than the surrounding fresh water.
In salt water, the melted ice will be less dense than the salt water, causing the dye to rise to the top.
Conclude that the color will settle at the bottom in fresh water and float to the top in salt water.

text: Which of the following is a Bronsted base, but not an Arrhenius [ah-REE-nee-us] base?
explainAnswer: Understand that a Bronsted base is a substance that can accept protons (H+), while an Arrhenius base produces hydroxide ions (OH-) in water.
Identify which of the given substances can accept protons; Triethylamine is a nitrogen-containing compound that can accept protons.
Check if the other options produce hydroxide ions in water: Sodium carbonate, Lithium hydroxide, and Potassium oxide all do.
Conclude that Triethylamine is a Bronsted base because it accepts protons but does not produce hydroxide ions, distinguishing it from Arrhenius bases.

text: When calculating the equilibrium constant for a reaction, the concentration of which of the following is generally included?
explainAnswer: Understand that the equilibrium constant expression is based on the concentrations of reactants and products.
Identify that only substances that are in a dynamic equilibrium (gases and solutes) are included in the expression.
Recognize that pure solids and pure liquids do not change concentration and are therefore excluded.
Conclude that solutes, which are in solution and can change concentration, are included in the equilibrium constant calculation.

text: Which of the following ions has the smallest radius?
explainAnswer: Identify the charge of each ion: Lithium ion (Li+), Beryllium ion (Be2+), Nitride (N3-), and Fluoride (F-).
Recognize that cations (positively charged ions) are generally smaller than their neutral atoms due to loss of electrons and increased nuclear charge.
Compare the sizes of the cations: Li+ has one less electron than neutral lithium, Be2+ has two less electrons than neutral beryllium.
Note that Be2+ has a higher positive charge than Li+, resulting in a stronger attraction to the remaining electrons, thus making it smaller.
Conclude that among the given ions, the Beryllium ion (Be2+) has the smallest radius.

text: An electron in the second main energy level and the second sublevel of an atom is described by which of the following orbital designations?
explainAnswer: Identify the main energy level, which is indicated by the first number in the designation.
Recognize that the second main energy level corresponds to n=2.
Determine the sublevel, which is indicated by the letter; 'p' represents the second sublevel.
Combine the main energy level and sublevel to form the correct designation: 2p.

text: What impurity found in coal contributes to acid rain?
explainAnswer: Identify the environmental impact of coal combustion.
Recall that certain impurities in coal can lead to the formation of acid rain.
Recognize that sulfur compounds can react with oxygen and water in the atmosphere to form sulfuric acid.
Eliminate the other choices based on their known contributions to acid rain.
Conclude that sulfur is the correct answer as it is the primary impurity in coal that contributes to acid rain.

text: Which of the following is the function of the carbon rod that runs down the center of a dry cell?
choices: To keep the chemical paste moist
To conduct electrons between materials involved in the chemical reaction
To break a circuit if it overheats
explainAnswer: Identify the components of a dry cell and their functions.
Understand that the carbon rod is a conductor within the cell.
Recognize that the primary role of a conductor is to facilitate the flow of electrons.
Eliminate other options that do not align with the function of conducting electrons.

text: MTBE or methyl tertiary butyl ether, is a:
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical structure and properties of MTBE.
Research the common uses of MTBE in various industries.
Eliminate options that do not align with the known applications of MTBE.
Confirm that MTBE is primarily used as a gasoline additive to improve combustion efficiency.

text: Organic compounds known as amines are so-named because they possess what element aside from carbon and hydrogen?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of amines in organic chemistry.
Recall that amines are derivatives of ammonia.
Recognize that ammonia (NH3) contains nitrogen as a key element.
Conclude that nitrogen is the element present in amines aside from carbon and hydrogen.

text: Fires are categorized by class. What type of fire is a class C fire?
explainAnswer: Understand that fires are classified into different categories based on their fuel sources.
Recall the classification system for fires, which includes Class A, B, C, D, and K.
Identify that Class C fires specifically involve electrical equipment or appliances.
Conclude that a Class C fire is therefore categorized as an electrical fire.

text: To the nearest degree Celsius, what temperature is absolute zero?
explainAnswer: Understand that absolute zero is the theoretical lowest temperature possible.
Know that absolute zero is defined as 0 Kelvin.
Convert 0 Kelvin to Celsius using the formula: Celsius = Kelvin - 273.15.
Round -273.15 to the nearest degree Celsius, which is -273.

text: What is the most stable isotope of rutherfordium (read as: ruh-the(r)-FOHR-dee-uhm)?
explainAnswer: Identify the element rutherfordium and its atomic number, which is 104.
Research the isotopes of rutherfordium and their respective atomic masses.
Determine the stability of each isotope by comparing their half-lives.
Identify RUTHERFORDIUM-267 as the isotope with the longest half-life, indicating it is the most stable.

text: What is the term for a compound that is composed of only carbon and hydrogen and contains one or more double bonds between carbon atoms?
explainAnswer: Identify the elements present in the compound, which are carbon and hydrogen.
Determine the type of bonding between the carbon atoms, focusing on the presence of double bonds.
Recognize that compounds with only carbon and hydrogen and at least one double bond are classified as alkenes.
Conclude that the term for such a compound is alkene.

text: What is the molecular formula for magnesium chloride?
explainAnswer: Identify the elements involved: magnesium (Mg) and chlorine (Cl).
Determine the charge of magnesium, which is +2 in ionic compounds.
Determine the charge of chlorine, which is -1 in ionic compounds.
Balance the charges by using two chlorine atoms to neutralize one magnesium atom.
Write the molecular formula as MgCl2.

text: The bubbles in boiling water are composed of what molecules?
explainAnswer: Recognize that boiling water involves the transition of water from liquid to gas.
Understand that the bubbles formed during boiling are actually water vapor.
Identify that water is composed of H2O molecules.
Conclude that the bubbles in boiling water are primarily made up of water (H2O).

text: When do water molecules move back and forth between the liquid and the gaseous state?
choices: Only when the air is saturated
Only when the outward movement of vapor molecules produces a pressure equal to the atmospheric pressure
explainAnswer: Understand that water molecules can evaporate and condense at any temperature, not just at boiling point.
Recognize that evaporation occurs when molecules gain enough energy to break free from the liquid state.
Acknowledge that condensation happens when vapor molecules lose energy and return to the liquid state.
Realize that these processes happen continuously, regardless of the saturation of air or external pressure conditions.

text: What law relates the force applied by a spring to its deformation?
explainAnswer: Identify the relationship between force and deformation in springs.
Recall that the deformation of a spring is proportional to the force applied.
Recognize that this relationship is described by Hooke's Law.
State Hooke's Law mathematically as F = kx, where F is the force, k is the spring constant, and x is the deformation.

text: Which of the following substances has the highest heat of vaporization?
explainAnswer: Understand that heat of vaporization is the amount of energy required to convert a substance from liquid to gas at its boiling point.
Recall that hydrogen bonding in water contributes to its relatively high heat of vaporization compared to other substances.
Compare the known values of heat of vaporization for ethanol, mercury, hexane, and water.
Identify that water has a higher heat of vaporization than the other listed substances.

text: Which of the following is NOT true with regard to the organization of the periodic table?
choices: Elements are grouped into their natural states as solids, liquids, and gases
Elements are in order of increasing atomic number
Elements are grouped into metals, metalloids, and nonmetals
Elements are divided into periods, groups, and series
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of the periodic table based on common knowledge.
Evaluate each choice to determine if it accurately describes the organization of the periodic table.
Recognize that while elements can exist as solids, liquids, or gases, they are not organized in the periodic table based on these states.
Conclude that the statement about grouping elements by their natural states is the one that is NOT true.

text: The finer a coffee bean is ground, the stronger the coffee will taste after brewing. This is BEST explained by an increase in the ground coffee beans:
explainAnswer: Identify the relationship between the grind size of coffee beans and the strength of the brewed coffee.
Consider how the size of the coffee particles affects the extraction process during brewing.
Recognize that smaller particles have a larger total surface area compared to larger particles.
Conclude that an increase in surface area allows for more efficient extraction of flavors and compounds, leading to a stronger taste.

text: As an atom’s atomic mass increases, more of what type of particles are needed to maintain nuclear stability:
explainAnswer: Understand that atomic mass is primarily determined by the number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Recognize that protons are positively charged and repel each other due to electromagnetic forces.
Know that neutrons are neutral particles that help to stabilize the nucleus by providing an attractive force without adding to the repulsion.
Conclude that as the number of protons increases (higher atomic mass), more neutrons are required to maintain stability in the nucleus.

text: Which of the following elements is contained in least significant concentrations in manganese nodules found on the ocean floor?
explainAnswer: Identify the elements listed in the choices: Iron, Plutonium, Nickel, and Manganese.
Research the composition of manganese nodules to understand the typical elements found in significant concentrations.
Compare the common concentrations of each element in manganese nodules.
Determine which element is least likely to be found in significant amounts based on the research.
Conclude that Plutonium is the element contained in the least significant concentrations.

text: Which of the following is NOT a base unit of measure in the metric system?
explainAnswer: Identify the base units of measure in the metric system, which include meter, second, ampere, and kilogram.
Recognize that the gram is a derived unit, as it is based on the kilogram.
Compare the options given to determine which one is not a base unit.
Conclude that the gram is the correct answer as it is not a base unit.

text: How many electron does the s subshell of an atom hold?
explainAnswer: Identify that the s subshell is the first subshell in the electron configuration of an atom.
Recall that each orbital can hold a maximum of 2 electrons.
Recognize that the s subshell contains only one orbital.
Multiply the number of orbitals in the s subshell (1) by the maximum number of electrons per orbital (2).
Conclude that the s subshell can hold a total of 2 electrons.

text: What is the name of the process in which nitrogen from dead and decomposing animals is converted to inorganic forms such as ammonium salts?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms related to nitrogen cycling in ecosystems.
Recall the processes involved in the breakdown of organic matter.
Determine which process specifically converts organic nitrogen into inorganic forms.
Match the identified process with its correct terminology.

text: A fifty-fifty solution of distilled water and pure ethanol will appear:
explainAnswer: Understand that a fifty-fifty solution means equal parts distilled water and pure ethanol.
Recognize that both distilled water and ethanol are clear liquids.
Consider that when mixed, the solution will not form any visible particles or layers.
Conclude that the resulting solution will appear clear.

text: Which of the following terms describes the relationship between L-ascorbic acid and D-ascorbic acid?
explainAnswer: Identify the structural differences between L-ascorbic acid and D-ascorbic acid.
Determine if the compounds are mirror images of each other.
Check if they are non-superimposable, which is a characteristic of enantiomers.
Confirm that they have the same molecular formula but differ in configuration at one or more chiral centers.

text: Butyric [byoo-TEER-ik] acid can condense with ethanol to produce an ester and what other molecule?
explainAnswer: Identify the reaction type, which is a condensation reaction between butyric acid and ethanol.
Recognize that in a condensation reaction, two molecules combine to form a larger molecule while releasing a smaller molecule.
Determine the smaller molecule released during the reaction, which is typically water when an acid reacts with an alcohol.
Conclude that the other molecule produced alongside the ester is water.

text: Elements are often classified by their atomic number. The atomic number denotes the number of:
explainAnswer: Understand that the atomic number is a fundamental property of an element.
Recall that the atomic number specifically indicates the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
Eliminate the other choices by recognizing that they do not accurately describe the atomic number.
Conclude that the correct answer is the number of protons per atom.

text: The cesium atom is used to define which of the following SI units?
explainAnswer: Recall that the definition of the second is based on the vibrations of the cesium atom.

Understand that the SI unit of time, the second, is defined as the duration of 9,192,631,770 periods of the radiation corresponding to the transition between two hyperfine levels of the ground state of the cesium-133 atom.
Eliminate the other options by recognizing that the meter is defined by the speed of light, the gram is defined by a specific mass, and the lumen is a measure of luminous flux.
Conclude that the correct answer is the second, as it is directly related to the cesium atom.

text: Which of the following is a property of carbon that makes it most effective as a polymer building block:
choices: it is in period 2 of the Periodic Table
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of carbon listed in the choices.
Understand the significance of a valence of 4 in terms of bonding.
Recognize that a valence of 4 allows carbon to form stable covalent bonds with multiple atoms.
Conclude that this property makes carbon an effective building block for polymers.

text: During a head-on car collision, what physical quantity remains constant for all passengers not wearing seat belts?
explainAnswer: Identify the scenario of a head-on car collision and the conditions affecting passengers.
Recognize that passengers not wearing seat belts are not restrained and will continue moving at the car's speed until acted upon by another force.
Apply Newton's first law of motion, which states that an object in motion stays in motion at a constant speed unless acted upon by an external force.
Conclude that the speed of the passengers remains constant until they collide with another object, such as the dashboard or windshield.

text: Which of the following does the subscript 3 indicate in the molecular formula for calcium carbonate?
choices: There are 3 oxygen atoms in one molecule of calcium carbonate
There are 3 carbon atoms in one molecule of calcium carbonate
There are 3 calcium atoms in one molecule of calcium carbonate
There are 3 atoms each of oxygen, carbon and calcium in one molecule of calcium carbonate
explainAnswer: Identify the molecular formula of calcium carbonate, which is CaCO3.
Recognize that the subscript indicates the number of atoms of the element it follows.
Note that the subscript '3' follows the oxygen (O) in the formula.
Conclude that the subscript '3' indicates there are 3 oxygen atoms in one molecule of calcium carbonate.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of the bonding ability of elements with no formal charge: 1) Hydrogen typically makes two bonds; 2) Oxygen typically makes two bonds; 3) Nitrogen typically makes four bonds.
explainAnswer: Identify the typical bonding patterns of hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen based on their valence electrons.
Recall that hydrogen has one valence electron and typically forms one bond.
Recognize that oxygen has six valence electrons and typically forms two bonds to achieve a full octet.
Note that nitrogen has five valence electrons and typically forms three bonds, not four.

text: In 1986, the Chernobyl nuclear power plant released several radioactive isotopes into the environment. Which of the following radioactive isotopes is most likely to have replaced the calcium in the bones of people who lived near Chernobyl?
explainAnswer: Identify the isotopes listed in the choices and their chemical properties.
Recognize that strontium is chemically similar to calcium and can replace it in biological systems.
Consider the context of radioactive isotopes released during the Chernobyl disaster and their effects on human health.
Eliminate the other options based on their chemical behavior and relevance to bone accumulation.

text: What is the most abundant element dissolved in ocean water?
explainAnswer: Recall that ocean water is a solution primarily composed of salts.
Identify the major components of seawater, which include various ions.
Recognize that sodium and chlorine are the most abundant ions in seawater, forming sodium chloride (table salt).
Determine that chlorine, as an ion, is more abundant than the other listed elements in ocean water.

text: Which of the following elements possesses the highest ionization energy?
explainAnswer: Recall that ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron from an atom.
Understand that ionization energy generally increases across a period in the periodic table due to increasing nuclear charge.
Identify that Neon is a noble gas located in Group 18, which typically has the highest ionization energies.
Compare the positions of Oxygen, Silicon, and Chlorine in relation to Neon, noting that they all have lower ionization energies than noble gases.

text: Which of the following molecules has the highest dipole moments?
explainAnswer: Identify the electronegativity values of the atoms involved in each molecule.
Determine the difference in electronegativity between hydrogen and the other halogens (fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine).
Recognize that a larger electronegativity difference indicates a stronger dipole moment.
Compare the calculated dipole moments and identify that hydrogen fluoride has the largest difference in electronegativity.

text: What functional group can be found in acetyl-salicylic acid that is not found in salicylic acid?
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical structures of both acetyl-salicylic acid and salicylic acid.
Look for the functional groups present in each compound.
Compare the functional groups in acetyl-salicylic acid with those in salicylic acid.
Determine which functional group is present in acetyl-salicylic acid but absent in salicylic acid.
Conclude that the functional group unique to acetyl-salicylic acid is the ester.

text: If an atom of gold has an atomic number of 79 and an atomic mass of 197, how many protons and neutrons are in the nucleus?
explainAnswer: Identify that the atomic number represents the number of protons in the atom.
Since the atomic number of gold is 79, it has 79 protons.
Use the atomic mass to find the number of neutrons by subtracting the atomic number from the atomic mass.
Calculate the number of neutrons: 197 (atomic mass) - 79 (protons) = 118 neutrons.

text: Sterling silver contains 92.5% silver and 7.5% copper. Which of the following substances is the solute?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of sterling silver, which are silver and copper.
Determine which component is present in a smaller amount, which indicates it is the solute.
Recognize that in sterling silver, copper is 7.5% and silver is 92.5%.
Conclude that since copper is in the lesser amount, it is the solute.

text: How many electrons does argon have in its valence electron shell?
explainAnswer: Identify the atomic number of argon, which is 18.
Determine the electron configuration of argon, which is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶.
Count the electrons in the outermost shell (n=3), which includes 3s and 3p subshells.
Add the electrons in the 3s (2) and 3p (6) subshells to find the total in the valence shell.
Conclude that argon has 8 valence electrons.

text: Solvated electrons appear a vibrant blue in solution. Which of the following colors of light is being absorbed?
explainAnswer: Identify that the color of the solution indicates which color of light is absorbed.
Recognize that if the solution appears blue, it absorbs the complementary color of blue.
Determine the complementary color of blue, which is orange.
Conclude that the absorbed color of light is therefore orange.

text: What very common modern masonry construction material found in many large buildings was actually invented by the Romans?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of modern masonry construction materials.
Consider historical advancements in construction materials.
Recall significant contributions made by the Romans in architecture and engineering.
Determine which material has persisted into modern times and is widely used in large buildings.
Conclude that the material invented by the Romans is cement.

text: Which of the following is an example of a compound with an ionic bond?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of bonds in the given compounds.
Recall that ionic bonds typically form between metals and nonmetals.
Analyze each choice to determine if it contains a metal and a nonmetal.
Recognize that sodium sulfide contains sodium (a metal) and sulfide (a nonmetal), indicating an ionic bond.
Conclude that sodium sulfide is the correct answer.

text: Identify all of the following three ionic compounds that are readily soluble in water: 1) Lithium phosphate; 2) Silver nitrate; 3) Calcium hydroxide.
explainAnswer: Recall the solubility rules for ionic compounds in water.
Identify that all nitrates (like silver nitrate) are soluble in water.
Check the solubility of lithium phosphate and calcium hydroxide, which are generally insoluble or have limited solubility.
Conclude that only silver nitrate is readily soluble in water.

text: Which of the following chemical formulas gives an indication of the arrangement of atoms and bonds in a chemical compound:
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of each type of chemical formula: empirical, molecular, structural, and polyatomic.
Determine which type of formula provides detailed information about the arrangement of atoms and the types of bonds in a compound.
Recognize that the structural formula specifically illustrates how atoms are connected and arranged in the molecule.
Conclude that the correct answer is the structural formula based on its definition and purpose.

text: How would you turn carbon-12 into the isotope carbon-13?
explainAnswer: Identify the difference between carbon-12 and carbon-13, which is the number of neutrons.
Carbon-12 has 6 neutrons, while carbon-13 has 7 neutrons.
Determine what needs to be added to carbon-12 to increase the neutron count from 6 to 7.
Conclude that adding a neutron will convert carbon-12 into carbon-13.

text: Isotopes of the same element are based on their different numbers of what atomic particle?
explainAnswer: Identify that isotopes are variants of the same element.
Recall that elements are defined by their number of protons.
Understand that isotopes differ in their number of neutrons.
Conclude that the difference in neutrons leads to different isotopes.

text: The electrical potential or power of a battery is an expression of its:
explainAnswer: Identify the terms related to electricity: amperage, resistance, conductivity, and voltage.
Understand that voltage is defined as the electrical potential difference between two points.
Recognize that amperage refers to the flow of electric current, resistance is the opposition to current flow, and conductivity is the ability of a material to conduct electricity.
Conclude that the term that directly relates to the electrical potential or power of a battery is voltage.

text: Which of the following electron configurations would be the most chemically stable?
explainAnswer: Identify the electron configurations provided in the choices.
Recall that the most stable electron configuration typically corresponds to a full outer shell.
Recognize that the configuration [He]2s^2 2p^6 has a full outer shell (2s and 2p orbitals are filled).
Compare this with the other configurations to see which ones have unfilled orbitals.
Conclude that [He]2s^2 2p^6 is the most chemically stable configuration.

text: The removal of silver tarnish by placing it in a bowl containing aluminum foil and a base is an example of which of the following types of reaction?
explainAnswer: Identify the process involved in removing silver tarnish, which typically involves a chemical reaction.
Recognize that tarnish is primarily silver sulfide (Ag2S) and that aluminum can reduce it back to silver.
Determine that in this reaction, silver is being reduced while aluminum is being oxidized, indicating a transfer of electrons.
Conclude that since there is a change in oxidation states for the elements involved, this is classified as a redox reaction.

text: Consider the reaction of A and B to yield 2C. In a reaction chamber, pure C is released and allowed to come to equilibrium. If the equilibrium constant is 625 and at equilibrium, there are 0.25 moles of C, then how many moles of A are there?
explainAnswer: Let the initial moles of A and B be x and y respectively, and at equilibrium, let the change in moles of A and B be -0.5z, where z is the moles of C produced.
Since 0.25 moles of C are present at equilibrium, we have z = 0.25, leading to a decrease of 0.5 * 0.25 = 0.125 moles for both A and B.
The equilibrium concentrations can be expressed as [A] = x - 0.125 and [B] = y - 0.125.
Using the equilibrium constant expression K = [C]^2 / ([A][B]), substitute K = 625 and [C] = 0.25 to find the relationship between x and y.
Solve the resulting equations to find the value of x, which represents the moles of A at equilibrium.

text: Spanky swings a ball on the end of a string and maintains it in uniform circular motion, what is the most accurate term for the force exerted on the rock through the string?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of motion involved, which is uniform circular motion.
Recognize that an object in uniform circular motion requires a force directed towards the center of the circle.
Understand that this inward force is necessary to keep the object moving in a circular path.
Conclude that the force exerted on the object through the string is called centripetal force.

text: What is the term for the process of removal of inorganic and organic substances from the “A” soil horizon by leaching?
explainAnswer: Identify the layers of soil and their characteristics.
Understand the process of leaching and how it affects soil composition.
Recognize the specific term used to describe the removal of materials from the soil horizon.
Match the definition of the process with the correct terminology.

text: What series of elements, which includes thorium, uranium, and plutonium, are characterized by having two outer 7s electrons?
explainAnswer: Identify the elements mentioned in the question: thorium, uranium, and plutonium.
Recognize that these elements are part of the periodic table and belong to a specific group based on their electron configuration.
Recall that actinides are the series of elements that include thorium, uranium, and plutonium, characterized by having their outermost electrons in the 7s subshell.
Eliminate the other choices by confirming that lanthanides, transition metals, and rare earth metals do not include these elements or do not fit the given description.

text: What inorganic nutrient, often found in detergent, is implicated in algal blooms?
explainAnswer: Identify common inorganic nutrients that can contribute to algal blooms.
Consider the sources of these nutrients, such as fertilizers and detergents.
Determine which of these nutrients is most commonly associated with detergents.
Recognize that phosphorus is a key nutrient that promotes algal growth.
Conclude that phosphorus is the inorganic nutrient implicated in algal blooms.

text: A carbohydrate contains 15 oxygen atoms. How many hydrogen atoms does it contain?
explainAnswer: Identify the general formula for carbohydrates, which is Cn(H2O)n.
Since there are 15 oxygen atoms, determine the number of water molecules, which is also 15.
Calculate the number of hydrogen atoms by multiplying the number of water molecules by 2, resulting in 30 hydrogen atoms.

text: On the Centigrade temperature scale give the whole number value that is the closest to absolute zero.
explainAnswer: Understand that absolute zero is the theoretical lowest temperature possible, where molecular motion stops.
Know that absolute zero is defined as 0 Kelvin.
Convert 0 Kelvin to Celsius using the formula: Celsius = Kelvin - 273.15.
Round -273.15 to the nearest whole number, which is -273.

text: How many nucleotide base pairs are there in the haploid human genome?
explainAnswer: Recall that the haploid human genome contains approximately 3 billion base pairs.
Recognize that the question asks for the haploid number, which is often simplified in options.
Convert 3 billion base pairs into millions by dividing by 1 million.
Identify that 3 billion base pairs is equal to 3,200 million base pairs.
Select the closest option to 3.2 billion base pairs, which is 3.2 million base pairs.

text: The formation of a mirage in the desert is an example of?
explainAnswer: Identify the phenomenon being described, which is the mirage in the desert.
Recall that a mirage occurs due to the bending of light rays.
Understand that this bending of light is caused by a change in the speed of light as it passes through different temperatures of air.
Conclude that this bending of light is an example of refraction.

text: Although none of the following are concrete proof of a chemical change, which of the following definitely could NOT be used as an indication that a chemical change has occurred?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics that indicate a chemical change, such as color change, heat production, and gas formation.
Evaluate each option to determine if it is a definitive indicator of a chemical change.
Recognize that a change in size can occur in both physical and chemical changes, making it not a definitive indicator.
Conclude that 'Change in size' is the only option that does not definitively indicate a chemical change.

text: Which of the following is NOT proper laboratory procedure:
choices: always read the upper edges of a meniscus when determining volume of water in a flask
the abbreviation TD on a pipette means ‘to deliver’
a borosilicate beaker is a better choice for heating a solution than one made of soda-lime
an analytical balance is more precise than a triple-beam balance
explainAnswer: Identify the proper laboratory procedures related to measuring volume and using equipment.
Review the definitions and functions of the terms used in the choices.
Evaluate each choice to determine if it aligns with standard laboratory practices.
Recognize that reading the upper edges of a meniscus is incorrect; the bottom of the meniscus should be read instead.
Select the choice that does not conform to proper laboratory procedure.

text: Which of the following foods contains the MOST milligrams of cholesterol:
explainAnswer: Identify the cholesterol content in each food item: cashew nuts (0 mg), whole egg (approximately 186 mg), whole milk (approximately 24 mg), and olive oil (0 mg).
Compare the cholesterol amounts to determine which food has the highest value.
Conclude that the whole egg contains the most cholesterol at approximately 186 mg.

text: Which of the following elements is a metalloid?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of a metalloid, which is an element that has properties of both metals and nonmetals.
Review the periodic table to locate the elements in the choices provided.
Determine which of the listed elements (Silicon, Calcium, Iron, Argon) falls under the category of metalloids.
Conclude that Silicon is the only element among the choices that is classified as a metalloid.

text: Where are the atoms with largest atomic radii found on the periodic table?
explainAnswer: Understand that atomic radius increases down a group and decreases across a period.
Identify that the lower left corner of the periodic table contains elements from Group 1 and Group 2, which have larger atomic radii.
Recognize that as you move down the groups, additional electron shells are added, increasing the size of the atoms.
Conclude that the largest atomic radii are found in the lower left corner of the periodic table.

text: Which of the following is NOT a transition metal?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of transition metals, which are elements found in the d-block of the periodic table.
Review the periodic table to locate each of the given elements: Aluminum, Zinc, Copper, and Manganese.
Determine which of the listed elements are found in the d-block; Zinc, Copper, and Manganese are transition metals.
Conclude that Aluminum, which is found in the p-block, is not a transition metal.

text: Which of the following molecules is an alkene?
explainAnswer: Identify the general formula for alkenes, which is CnH2n.
Count the number of carbon atoms in each option.
Calculate the corresponding number of hydrogen atoms using the alkene formula for each option.
Compare the calculated hydrogen counts with the given options to find a match.
Select the molecule that fits the alkene formula, which is C2H4.

text: According to VSEPR theory, what is the molecular geometry of methane?
explainAnswer: Identify the central atom in methane, which is carbon.
Count the number of bonding pairs of electrons around the central atom; methane has four hydrogen atoms bonded to carbon.
Determine the electron pair geometry based on the number of bonding pairs, which in this case is four.
Apply VSEPR theory to conclude that four bonding pairs result in a tetrahedral molecular geometry.

text: Solutions with a pH less than about 6 typically have what distinctive taste?
explainAnswer: Recall that pH is a measure of acidity or alkalinity in a solution.
Understand that lower pH values indicate higher acidity.
Identify that acidic solutions often have a sour taste.
Conclude that solutions with a pH less than about 6 typically taste sour.

text: Name all of the following 4 choices that are organic acids: citric acid; hydrochloric acid; nitric acid; hydrogen sulfide
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of organic acids, which are typically carbon-containing compounds that can donate protons (H+).
Evaluate each choice to determine if it contains carbon and fits the definition of an organic acid.
Recognize that citric acid is a carbon-containing compound and qualifies as an organic acid.
Conclude that hydrochloric acid, nitric acid, and hydrogen sulfide do not meet the criteria for organic acids.

text: Identify all of the following three gas laws that make the assumption that the pressure of a system is kept constant: 1) Boyle's; 2) Charles's; 3) Gay-Lussac's [LOO-sax].
explainAnswer: Recall the definitions of each gas law.
Boyle's Law relates pressure and volume at constant temperature.
Charles's Law relates volume and temperature at constant pressure.
Gay-Lussac's Law relates pressure and temperature at constant volume.
Identify which law specifically states that pressure is constant, which is Charles's Law.

text: If selenium has an atomic mass of 79, and an atomic number of 34, how many neutrons does it have?
explainAnswer: Identify the atomic mass of selenium, which is given as 79.
Identify the atomic number of selenium, which is given as 34.
Subtract the atomic number from the atomic mass to find the number of neutrons: 79 - 34.
Calculate the result, which gives you 45 neutrons.

text: An ideal gas with molar mass 26 is kept at 200 kelvins and at 4 atmospheres of pressure, and is found to have a density of 1.6 grams per liter. What is the density, in grams per liter, of a different ideal gas with molar mass 52 if it is at a temperature of 400 kelvins and a pressure of 2 atmospheres?
explainAnswer: Use the ideal gas law to relate density, pressure, temperature, and molar mass: density = (pressure * molar mass) / (R * temperature).
Calculate the density of the first gas using its given values: density = (4 atm * 26 g/mol) / (R * 200 K).
Use the same formula to find the density of the second gas with molar mass 52 at the new conditions: density = (2 atm * 52 g/mol) / (R * 400 K).
Simplify the expression for the second gas's density and substitute the known values to find the result.

text: Bases, when dissolved in water, have a pH value above what number?
explainAnswer: Understand that pH is a scale that measures the acidity or basicity of a solution.
Recognize that a pH value of 7 is considered neutral, which is the pH of pure water.
Know that bases are substances that increase the concentration of hydroxide ions (OH-) in a solution.
Conclude that when bases are dissolved in water, they will result in a pH value greater than 7.

text: Which of the following choices is NOT an example of a chemical change:
choices: shiny new copper tarnishing to a green color
bubbles forming in a solution of vinegar following the addition of baking soda
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of a chemical change, which typically involve a change in composition or the formation of new substances.
Analyze each choice to determine if it involves a change in chemical composition.
Recognize that shiny new copper tarnishing, bubbles from vinegar and baking soda, and iron rusting all involve chemical changes.
Note that steel turning red upon heating is a physical change, as it does not alter the chemical composition of the steel.

text: There are at least seven strong acids. Give the common names of five of them.
explainAnswer: Recall the definition of strong acids, which completely dissociate in water.
List common strong acids that are typically studied in chemistry.
Identify at least five strong acids from your list.
Verify that the acids you have chosen are indeed classified as strong acids.

text: What group of elements react violently with water and have one electron in their valence shell?
explainAnswer: Identify the group of elements that have one electron in their valence shell, which are the alkali metals.
Recall that alkali metals include lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, cesium, and francium.
Recognize that alkali metals react violently with water, producing hydrogen gas and heat.
Conclude that the group of elements that fits both criteria is the alkali metals.

text: What is the chemical name of Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>?
explainAnswer: Identify the elements present in the chemical formula Al2O3, which are aluminum (Al) and oxygen (O).
Determine the number of atoms of each element in the compound, which is 2 aluminum atoms and 3 oxygen atoms.
Combine the names of the elements with their respective quantities, using the prefix 'di-' for two aluminum atoms and 'tri-' for three oxygen atoms.
Since aluminum oxide is a common compound, it is referred to simply as aluminum oxide without the prefixes.

text: What is the chemical formula of ammonia?
explainAnswer: Identify that ammonia is a compound made of nitrogen and hydrogen.
Determine the number of nitrogen atoms in ammonia, which is 1.
Determine the number of hydrogen atoms in ammonia, which is 3.
Combine the symbols and the number of atoms to form the chemical formula, resulting in NH3.

text: In terms of hydronium ion concentration, how many times as concentrated is a solution of pH 4 as a solution of pH 7?
explainAnswer: Recall that pH is defined as the negative logarithm of the hydronium ion concentration: pH = -log[H3O+].
Calculate the hydronium ion concentration for pH 4: [H3O+] = 10^(-4) M.
Calculate the hydronium ion concentration for pH 7: [H3O+] = 10^(-7) M.
Divide the concentration at pH 4 by the concentration at pH 7: (10^(-4)) / (10^(-7)) = 10^(3).
Conclude that the solution of pH 4 is 1000 times more concentrated than the solution of pH 7.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of atomic theory: 1) Hydrogen gas has a mass of 1 AMU; 2) Compounds can contain any real number of atoms; 3) One liter of argon at STP contains the same number of atoms as one liter of neon at STP.
explainAnswer: Evaluate the mass of hydrogen gas in atomic mass units (AMU) and confirm that it is approximately 1 AMU.
Determine if compounds can contain any real number of atoms, recognizing that they must consist of whole atoms.

Recall that at standard temperature and pressure (STP), one mole of any gas occupies the same volume and contains the same number of molecules, thus one liter of argon contains the same number of atoms as one liter of neon.

text: Identify all of the following three types of radioactivity that when emitted by an atom, results in a change in its atomic number but NOT a change in its atomic mass number: 1) Alpha; 2) Beta; 3) Gamma.
explainAnswer: Understand that atomic number refers to the number of protons in an atom, while atomic mass number refers to the total number of protons and neutrons.
Recognize that alpha decay involves the emission of 2 protons and 2 neutrons, which changes both the atomic number and mass number.
Identify that beta decay involves the conversion of a neutron into a proton (or vice versa), which changes the atomic number but keeps the mass number the same.
Note that gamma decay involves the emission of energy without changing the number of protons or neutrons, thus not affecting either atomic number or mass number.
Conclude that only beta decay results in a change in atomic number without changing the atomic mass number.

text: Heating an endothermic reaction will shift equilibrium towards which of the following?
explainAnswer: Identify that an endothermic reaction absorbs heat, meaning heat is a reactant.
Apply Le Chatelier's principle, which states that if a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it will shift to counteract the disturbance.
Recognize that adding heat to an endothermic reaction will shift the equilibrium towards the products to absorb the added heat.
Conclude that the correct answer is 'The products' as the equilibrium shifts in that direction.

text: The reaction of hydrocarbons found in such things as wood and paper with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide, water and heat is called:
explainAnswer: Identify the key components of the reaction: hydrocarbons, oxygen, carbon dioxide, water, and heat.
Recall the definitions of the given choices: fission, fusion, endothermic, and combustion.
Recognize that the reaction described involves the burning of hydrocarbons in the presence of oxygen.
Determine that the process of burning hydrocarbons to produce energy is known as combustion.
Select 'combustion' as the correct answer based on the definitions and the context of the reaction.

text: What products are formed from the reaction of sodium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid?
explainAnswer: Identify the reactants: sodium hydroxide (NaOH) and hydrochloric acid (HCl).
Recognize that this is a neutralization reaction between an acid and a base.
Write the balanced chemical equation: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H2O.
Determine the products formed: sodium chloride (NaCl) and water (H2O).
Conclude that the products of the reaction are water and salt.

text: Which of the following is NOT a product of the Krebs, or tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle?
explainAnswer: Recall the main products of the Krebs cycle, which include ATP, NADH, and CO2.
Identify that H2O is not typically produced directly in the Krebs cycle.
Eliminate the other options as they are known products of the cycle.
Conclude that H2O is the correct answer as it is not a product of the Krebs cycle.

text: The molecular weight of sodium is 22.99 grams per mole, and the molecular weight of chlorine is 35.45 grams per mole. What is the molecular weight in grams per mole of sodium chloride?
explainAnswer: Identify the molecular weights of sodium (Na) and chlorine (Cl).
Add the molecular weight of sodium (22.99 g/mol) to the molecular weight of chlorine (35.45 g/mol).
Calculate the sum: 22.99 + 35.45.
The result is the molecular weight of sodium chloride (NaCl), which is 58.44 g/mol.

text: The lead-acid battery is most commonly found in:
explainAnswer: Identify the common applications of lead-acid batteries.
Consider the power requirements and size constraints of each option.
Recognize that lead-acid batteries are typically used for high power demands and larger sizes.
Determine that automobiles require reliable, high-capacity batteries for starting and powering electrical systems.
Conclude that automobiles are the most common application for lead-acid batteries.

text: When two different waves end up in the same location, they undergo what phenomenon that can either be constructive or destructive?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of wave behavior when multiple waves meet at the same point.
Understand that this phenomenon can result in either an increase in amplitude (constructive interference) or a decrease in amplitude (destructive interference).
Recall the terminology used to describe this phenomenon, which is known as interference.

text: Sulfuric acid is spilled on a laboratory bench. Which of the following chemicals would be useful for neutralizing the acid?
explainAnswer: Identify that sulfuric acid is a strong acid that needs to be neutralized.
Recall that a neutralizing agent should be a base.
Evaluate the given options to determine which one is a base.
Recognize that sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) is a common weak base used for neutralizing acids.
Conclude that sodium bicarbonate is the appropriate choice for neutralizing sulfuric acid.

text: Which of the following is the BEST example of a suspension:
choices: water with 10% ethanol added to it
table sugar completely dissolved in water
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of a suspension, which is a heterogeneous mixture where solid particles are dispersed in a liquid but not dissolved.
Evaluate each choice to see if it contains solid particles that can settle out over time.
Determine that water with 10% ethanol is a solution, olive oil in water is an emulsion, and table sugar dissolved in water is a solution.
Recognize that orange juice with pulp contains solid particles (pulp) suspended in the liquid, making it the best example of a suspension.

text: James Chadwick proposed that the nucleus contains not only protons, but what other subatomic particles?
explainAnswer: Recall the historical context of James Chadwick's work in the early 20th century.
Identify the components of the atomic nucleus that were known before Chadwick's discovery.
Recognize that protons were already established, and consider what other particles could exist in the nucleus.
Understand that Chadwick's experiments led to the discovery of a neutral particle that accounts for additional mass in the nucleus.
Conclude that the other subatomic particle proposed by Chadwick is neutrons.

text: Nitrogen has 7 protons. What is the atomic mass of its common isotope, rounded to the nearest whole number?
explainAnswer: Identify that nitrogen has 7 protons, which means its atomic number is 7.
Understand that the atomic mass of an element is primarily determined by the number of protons and neutrons in its nucleus.
Know that the most common isotope of nitrogen is nitrogen-14, which has 7 protons and 7 neutrons.
Add the number of protons and neutrons together: 7 protons + 7 neutrons = 14.
Conclude that the atomic mass of nitrogen's common isotope, rounded to the nearest whole number, is 14.

text: Brass is an alloy of which two metals?
explainAnswer: Recall the definition of an alloy and its components.
Identify common alloys and their constituent metals.
Recognize that brass is specifically known as an alloy of copper and zinc.
Eliminate the other choices based on known compositions of those alloys.

text: Which of the following four processes is endothermic?
explainAnswer: Identify the processes listed and understand their general characteristics.
Recall that an endothermic process absorbs heat from the surroundings.
Evaluate each process: combustion and explosion release heat, while condensation releases heat as well.
Recognize that melting ice requires heat absorption to change from solid to liquid, making it endothermic.
Conclude that the melting of ice cubes is the only endothermic process among the choices.

text: Identify all of the following three substances that can form hydrogen bonds: 1) Ammonia; 2) Argon; 3) Hydrogen bromide.
explainAnswer: Identify the presence of hydrogen atoms bonded to highly electronegative atoms (N, O, or F) in each substance.
Check if ammonia (NH3) has hydrogen atoms bonded to nitrogen, which is electronegative enough to form hydrogen bonds.
Determine that argon (Ar) is a noble gas and does not form hydrogen bonds due to lack of hydrogen or electronegative atoms.
Evaluate hydrogen bromide (HBr) to see that while it has hydrogen, bromine is not electronegative enough to facilitate hydrogen bonding.

text: Which reaction type occurs when an acid and base react to produce a salt and water?
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of the given reaction types: Acidification, Neutralization, Ammonification, and Basification.
Recall that an acid-base reaction typically produces a salt and water.
Recognize that the reaction producing a salt and water from an acid and base is defined as Neutralization.
Eliminate the other options based on their definitions and relevance to the reaction described.
Conclude that the correct answer is Neutralization.

text: What term refers to the tendency of an object to resist changes in motion?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept related to motion in physics.
Recall the definition of inertia as it pertains to an object's resistance to changes in its state of motion.
Recognize that inertia is a fundamental property of matter.
Conclude that the term you are looking for is inertia.

text: Name all of the following 3 substances that will likely form a weak electrolyte when dissolved in pure water: acetic acid; magnesium chloride; sodium hydroxide
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of strong and weak electrolytes.
Recall that strong electrolytes completely dissociate into ions in solution, while weak electrolytes only partially dissociate.
Evaluate each substance: acetic acid is a weak acid and does not fully dissociate, while magnesium chloride and sodium hydroxide are strong electrolytes that fully dissociate.
Conclude that acetic acid is the only substance that will likely form a weak electrolyte when dissolved in pure water.

text: Butane is made up of what 2 elements?
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical formula of butane, which is C4H10.
Recognize that the letters 'C' and 'H' in the formula represent the elements carbon and hydrogen.
Count the number of different elements present in the formula.
Conclude that butane is composed of carbon and hydrogen.

text: Stainless steel is differentiated from other steels based mainly on the content of what element?
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristics that differentiate stainless steel from other types of steel.
Research the chemical composition of stainless steel and its common elements.
Focus on the element that is present in higher amounts in stainless steel compared to other steels.
Conclude that chromium is the primary element responsible for the corrosion resistance of stainless steel.

text: According to valence bond theory, how many electrons are being shared between two atoms of fluorine in diatomic fluorine gas?
explainAnswer: Identify that diatomic fluorine gas consists of two fluorine atoms.
Recall that each fluorine atom has seven valence electrons.
Understand that in order to achieve a stable octet, each fluorine atom shares one electron with the other.
Conclude that the total number of electrons shared between the two fluorine atoms is two.

text: Consider a chemical reaction with a standard enthalpy change of 10 kilojoules per mole and a standard entropy change of 10 joules per mole kelvin. When is this reaction spontaneous?
explainAnswer: Identify the relationship between enthalpy change (ΔH), entropy change (ΔS), and temperature (T) using the Gibbs free energy equation: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS.
For the reaction to be spontaneous, ΔG must be less than 0, which leads to the inequality: ΔH - TΔS < 0.
Rearranging the inequality gives T > ΔH / ΔS.
Substitute the given values: T > 10 kJ/mol / 10 J/mol·K.
Convert units and solve for T to find that T > 1000 K.

text: Twenty grams of the following gases are each added to a container: oxygen, helium, water vapor, and xenon. Which of these gases would have the largest partial pressure under conditions of standard temperature and pressure?
explainAnswer: Identify the molar mass of each gas: oxygen (O2) is 32 g/mol, helium (He) is 4 g/mol, water vapor (H2O) is 18 g/mol, and xenon (Xe) is 131.3 g/mol.
Calculate the number of moles of each gas by dividing the mass (20 g) by the molar mass of each gas.
Use the ideal gas law, where partial pressure is proportional to the number of moles, to determine which gas has the highest number of moles.
Compare the number of moles calculated for each gas to find that helium has the highest number of moles, thus the largest partial pressure.

text: The acidity of a water sample with a pH of 5 is how many times as great as that of a sample with a pH of 6?
explainAnswer: Understand that pH is a logarithmic scale where each whole number change represents a tenfold change in acidity.
Recognize that a pH of 5 is one unit lower than a pH of 6.
Calculate the difference in pH, which is 1 unit.
Since each unit change in pH corresponds to a factor of 10, conclude that the acidity of the sample with pH 5 is 10 times greater than that of pH 6.

text: Which of the following is a molecular triatomic compound with a linear molecular shape?
explainAnswer: Identify the molecular shape of each compound listed in the choices.
Recall that a linear molecular shape occurs when there are no lone pairs on the central atom and the surrounding atoms are arranged in a straight line.
Analyze the molecular structure of each compound: Water is bent, Calcium chloride is ionic, Hydrogen peroxide is not linear.
Determine that Carbon dioxide has a linear shape with the structure O=C=O, confirming it is the correct answer.

text: Why do many bridges have expansion joints?
choices: To reduce the vibration of cars traveling across the bridge
To permit quick disassembly in case of flooding or other disasters
To increase resistance to UVB-induced photo-degradation
To prevent buckling when the bridge expands and contracts with temperature changes
explainAnswer: Identify the purpose of expansion joints in structures.
Consider how temperature changes affect materials, particularly metals and concrete.
Evaluate each choice to see which one relates to the effects of thermal expansion and contraction.
Select the answer that directly addresses the prevention of structural issues due to temperature changes.

text: Which of the following is NOT true regarding one mole of two different stable isotopes of the same atom?
choices: Both have the same number of molecules
If used in the same chemical reaction, both produce the same number of moles of products
Both have the same number of protons
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of isotopes, noting that they have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Recognize that the difference in neutrons results in different atomic masses for each isotope.
Evaluate the choices based on the properties of isotopes, confirming that they will have the same number of molecules and protons, but different masses.
Conclude that the statement 'Both have the same mass' is NOT true, as it contradicts the definition of isotopes.

text: Which of the following is a strong acid?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of strong acids, which completely dissociate in water.
Review the list of acids provided and recall their strengths.
Recognize that sulfuric acid is known for its strong acidic properties compared to the others listed.
Conclude that sulfuric acid is the correct answer as it is a strong acid.

text: When a substance contains more of a dissolved compound than can be dissolved by the solvent under standard conditions, it is referred to as which of the following?
explainAnswer: Understand the definitions of the terms related to solubility: saturated, unsaturated, and supersaturated.
Identify that a saturated solution contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve at a given temperature.
Recognize that a supersaturated solution contains more solute than can normally dissolve under standard conditions.
Eliminate the other options by confirming they do not fit the definition of having more solute than can be dissolved.

text: Calculate the density of an object, in grams per cubic centimeter, from the following information: When an object with a mass of 25 grams is placed in a graduated cylinder filled with water, the water lever changes from 12.8 to 15.3 cubic centimeters.
explainAnswer: Determine the volume of the object by subtracting the initial water level from the final water level in the graduated cylinder.
Calculate the volume: 15.3 cm³ - 12.8 cm³ = 2.5 cm³.
