text: Giving the proper charges, what are the chemical formulas for the major ions present in a aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide, or NaOH?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of sodium hydroxide, which are sodium (Na) and hydroxide (OH).
Determine the charge of sodium, which is +1, and the charge of hydroxide, which is -1.
Recognize that in an aqueous solution, sodium exists as Na+ and hydroxide as OH-.
List the major ions present in the solution, which are Na+ and OH-.

text: Rank the following three elements in terms of increasing atomic mass: 1) Cesium; 2) Copper; 3) Lithium.
explainAnswer: Identify the atomic masses of each element: Lithium (Li) is approximately 6.94 u, Copper (Cu) is approximately 63.55 u, and Cesium (Cs) is approximately 132.91 u.
List the elements with their atomic masses: Lithium (6.94 u), Copper (63.55 u), Cesium (132.91 u).
Compare the atomic masses to determine their order from smallest to largest: Lithium < Copper < Cesium.
Rank the elements in increasing order of atomic mass: Lithium (3), Copper (2), Cesium (1).

text: Acids are often defined as proton donors. Which of the following is the common form of this proton:
explainAnswer: Recall the definition of acids as proton donors.
Identify the common form of a proton in chemical terms.
Recognize that a proton is equivalent to a positive hydrogen ion (H+).
Eliminate the other choices that do not represent a proton.

text: Ejecting electrons from the ground state of a metal atom typically requires light from which of the following regions of the electromagnetic spectrum?
explainAnswer: Understand that ejecting electrons from a metal atom requires energy input that can overcome the work function of the metal.
Recall that the energy of a photon is related to its frequency, with higher frequency photons carrying more energy.
Identify that X-rays have a high frequency and therefore high energy, making them capable of ejecting electrons from the ground state of metal atoms.
Eliminate the other options (Radio, Infrared, Visible) as they have lower energy and are insufficient to cause electron ejection.

text: What ion is known as the stable identity of the proton?
explainAnswer: Identify that the stable identity of a proton refers to its simplest form.
Recognize that a proton is a positively charged particle found in the nucleus of an atom.
Understand that when a hydrogen atom loses its electron, it becomes a hydrogen ion (H+).
Conclude that the hydrogen ion is essentially a proton, making it the stable identity of the proton.

text: Carbon has three isotopes: carbon-12, carbon-13, and carbon-14. How many protons are in the nucleus [NOO-klee-uhs] of these carbon atoms, respectively?
explainAnswer: Identify that isotopes of an element have the same number of protons.
Recall that the atomic number of carbon is 6.
Conclude that all isotopes of carbon (carbon-12, carbon-13, carbon-14) have 6 protons in their nuclei.

text: Which of the following is the term for the transfer of energy through matter by the collision of atoms in a material?
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of each term provided in the choices.
Recognize that conduction specifically refers to energy transfer through direct contact between atoms.
Eliminate options that do not involve direct atomic collisions, such as convection and radiation.
Select conduction as the correct answer since it matches the definition of energy transfer through matter by atomic collision.

text: Identify the reactant or reactants that are oxidized in the reaction: Zn + 2HCl → Zn<sup>2+</sup> + H<sub>2</sub> + 2Cl<sup>−</sup> ?
explainAnswer: Identify the oxidation states of each element in the reactants and products.
Determine which element undergoes an increase in oxidation state, indicating oxidation.
In this reaction, zinc (Zn) goes from 0 to +2, showing it is oxidized.
Conclude that zinc is the reactant that is oxidized.

text: Identify all of the following three compounds that consist of only carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen: 1) Glucose; 2) Ethanol; 3) Acetic acid.
explainAnswer: List the chemical formulas of each compound: Glucose (C6H12O6), Ethanol (C2H5OH), Acetic acid (C2H4O2).
Identify the elements present in each formula: all three contain only carbon (C), hydrogen (H), and oxygen (O).
Confirm that there are no other elements in the formulas provided.
Conclude that all three compounds consist solely of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

text: How many electrons are present in nitrogen-14, when nitrogen as atomic number seven is in its three minus oxidation state?
explainAnswer: Identify the atomic number of nitrogen, which is 7, indicating it has 7 protons and, in its neutral state, 7 electrons.
Determine the oxidation state of nitrogen, which is given as three minus (-3).
Calculate the total number of electrons by adding the oxidation state to the number of protons: 7 protons + 3 additional electrons = 10 electrons.

text: Identify all of the following diatomic species that contain covalent bonds: 1) Potassium chloride; 2) Molecular chlorine; 3) Sodium fluoride.
explainAnswer: Identify the nature of the bonds in each diatomic species.
Potassium chloride (KCl) is an ionic compound, so it does not contain covalent bonds.
Molecular chlorine (Cl2) consists of two chlorine atoms sharing electrons, indicating a covalent bond.
Sodium fluoride (NaF) is also an ionic compound, so it does not contain covalent bonds.
Conclude that the only diatomic species with covalent bonds is molecular chlorine (Cl2).

text: Which of the following does NOT depend on a chemical reaction?
choices: Your voice squeaking when you breathe helium
Fizzing of an Alka-Seltzer in water
explainAnswer: Identify the processes associated with each option.
Determine if each process involves a chemical change or reaction.
Recognize that your voice squeaking when you breathe helium is a physical change, not a chemical reaction.
Conclude that the correct answer is the option that does not involve a chemical reaction.

text: What is the name of the principle that states that no more than two electrons can occupy any one orbital, and that if two electrons occupy the same orbital, then their spins must be paired?
explainAnswer: Identify the principle related to electron configuration in atomic orbitals.
Recall the rules governing electron occupancy in orbitals.
Recognize that the principle specifies the maximum number of electrons per orbital.
Understand that if two electrons share an orbital, their spins must be opposite.
Conclude that this principle is known as the Pauli Exclusion Principle.

text: What is the term for a molecule that is composed of a very large number of individual monomers bonded together?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of a molecule composed of repeating units.
Recall the term used for a single unit that can join together with others.
Combine the knowledge of the repeating units to determine the term for the large molecule.
Conclude that the term for a molecule made of many monomers is 'polymer'.

text: How many nodes are found in a 1s orbital?
explainAnswer: Understand that a 1s orbital is a type of atomic orbital that can hold electrons.
Recognize that the term 'nodes' refers to regions where the probability of finding an electron is zero.
Identify that the 1s orbital has no angular nodes and only one radial node.
Conclude that since the radial node is not present in the 1s orbital, the total number of nodes is zero.

text: What is the term for a pair of non-bonding electrons in a molecule?
explainAnswer: Recall the definition of electron pairs in a molecule.
Identify the difference between bonding and non-bonding electrons.
Recognize that non-bonding electrons are those that are not involved in forming bonds between atoms.
Conclude that a pair of non-bonding electrons is specifically referred to as a 'lone pair'.

text: Rank the following three elements in order of increasing atomic radius: 1) Magnesium; 2) Silicon; 3) Chlorine.
explainAnswer: Identify the position of each element in the periodic table: Magnesium (Mg) is in group 2, Silicon (Si) is in group 14, and Chlorine (Cl) is in group 17.
Recognize that atomic radius generally decreases across a period from left to right due to increasing nuclear charge.
Note that atomic radius increases down a group due to the addition of electron shells.
Rank the elements based on their positions: Chlorine has the smallest radius, followed by Silicon, and Magnesium has the largest radius.

text: Which of the following could be used to neutralize an acid spill?
explainAnswer: Identify the nature of the substances listed in the choices.
Determine which substances are basic or alkaline, as they can neutralize acids.
Calcium oxide is known to be a strong base and can effectively neutralize acids.
Eliminate the other options that do not have neutralizing properties for acids.

text: By number, identify all of the following three statements that are TRUE about catalysts: 1) they change the rate of the reaction, 2) they change the chemical equilibrium of the reaction, 3) they decrease the activation energy.
explainAnswer: Understand that catalysts speed up reactions without being consumed, which affects the rate of the reaction.
Recognize that catalysts do not change the overall chemical equilibrium of a reaction; they only help reach equilibrium faster.
Know that catalysts lower the activation energy required for a reaction to occur, facilitating the reaction process.

text: Halite is composed of what two elements?
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical formula of halite, which is NaCl.
Recognize that Na represents sodium and Cl represents chlorine.
Conclude that halite is composed of sodium and chlorine.

text: In an atom, what is the maximum number of electrons the first energy level can hold?
explainAnswer: Identify that the first energy level corresponds to the principal quantum number n=1.
Recall the formula for the maximum number of electrons in an energy level, which is given by 2n^2.
Substitute n=1 into the formula to calculate the maximum number of electrons: 2(1^2).
Calculate the result, which is 2, indicating the maximum number of electrons the first energy level can hold.

text: A chemist is trying to pick a weak base for performing a titration. Which of the following could she choose?
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of weak bases, which are typically not fully ionized in solution.
Review the list of choices to determine which compounds are bases.
Recognize that potassium hydroxide is a strong base, while potassium chloride and sodium chloride are neutral salts.
Determine that potassium acetate is a salt derived from a weak acid (acetic acid) and a strong base (potassium hydroxide), making it a weak base.

text: Which of the following does NOT include a chemical reaction?
choices: Immersing an iron nail in a copper sulfate solution to coat the nail with copper metal
Combining water, rocks and gravel with cement to make concrete
Combining copper and tin to make bronze
explainAnswer: Identify which processes involve a change in chemical composition.
Making caramel from sugar involves heating sugar, causing a chemical change.
Immersing an iron nail in copper sulfate leads to a chemical reaction where copper is deposited on the nail.
Combining water, rocks, and gravel with cement results in a chemical reaction as the cement hardens.
Combining copper and tin is a physical mixture without a chemical reaction, thus it does not change the chemical properties of the elements.

text: A carboxyl group is the functional group in which of the following classes of compounds:
explainAnswer: Identify the structure of a carboxyl group, which is -COOH.
Recall that organic acids are characterized by the presence of a carboxyl group.
Evaluate the other options: esters contain a carboxyl group but are derived from organic acids, halocarbons do not contain a carboxyl group, and hydrocarbons consist only of carbon and hydrogen.
Conclude that the only class of compounds that directly contains a carboxyl group is organic acid.

text: Which of the following is the BEST example of a chemical reaction:
choices: an acid is added to a clear solution in a test tube and a white substance appears and falls to the bottom of the test tube
milk is added to water and the water turns a milky color
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of a chemical reaction, which typically involves the formation of new substances.
Evaluate each choice to see if it describes a process that results in new substances being formed.
Consider the first choice where an acid reacts with a solution to produce a white precipitate, indicating a new substance has formed.
Compare this with the other choices, which either involve physical changes or do not produce new substances.
Conclude that the first choice is the best example of a chemical reaction.

text: What atomic particle is most directly responsible for fissioning each nucleus in an atomic chain reaction?
explainAnswer: Identify the process of fission and its requirements.
Understand that fission occurs when a nucleus absorbs a particle and becomes unstable.
Recognize that neutrons are neutral particles that can penetrate the nucleus without repulsion.
Conclude that neutrons are the particles that initiate the fission process in a chain reaction.

text: Which of the following elements exists in nature?
explainAnswer: Identify the elements listed in the choices.
Research the natural occurrence of each element.
Determine which of the elements is known to exist in nature without artificial synthesis.
Conclude that Protactinium is the only element among the choices that occurs naturally.

text: Which of the following is closest to the ratio of nitrogen molecules to oxygen molecules in the air?
explainAnswer: Understand that the composition of air is approximately 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.
Convert these percentages into a ratio by comparing the amounts of nitrogen to oxygen.
Calculate the ratio of nitrogen to oxygen as 78:21.
Simplify the ratio by dividing both numbers by 21, resulting in approximately 3.71:1.
Recognize that 3.71:1 is closest to the ratio 4:1 among the given choices.

text: According to VSEPR [VESS-pur] theory, what is the molecular geometry of water?
explainAnswer: Identify the central atom in the water molecule, which is oxygen.
Count the number of bonding pairs and lone pairs of electrons around the central atom.
Apply VSEPR theory, which states that electron pairs will arrange themselves to minimize repulsion.
Determine the molecular geometry based on the arrangement of the bonding pairs and lone pairs, which in this case results in a bent shape.

text: When an Arrhenius [ahr-RAY-nee-oos] acid is added to a base, what are the products?
explainAnswer: Identify that an Arrhenius acid produces hydrogen ions (H+) in solution.
Recognize that a base produces hydroxide ions (OH-) in solution.
Combine the H+ from the acid with the OH- from the base to form water (H2O).
Identify the remaining ions from the acid and base, which combine to form a salt.

text: Which of the following is the BEST description of a colloid:
choices: a homogeneous mixture of uniform particles in solution
a mixture of different substances that never settle out of solution
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of a colloid, which include the presence of different substances that do not settle out.
Evaluate each choice to see which one aligns with the definition of a colloid.
Eliminate options that describe solutions or mixtures that do not fit the colloid definition.
Select the choice that accurately describes a colloid as a mixture of different substances that remain suspended.

text: Which of the following is the minimum amount of energy needed to start a chemical reaction?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which is about the energy required to initiate a chemical reaction.
Review the definitions of the provided choices: Production, Reaction, Activation, and Catalytic.
Recognize that 'Activation' energy specifically refers to the minimum energy needed to start a reaction.
Eliminate the other options based on their definitions and relevance to the question.
Conclude that 'Activation' is the correct answer.

text: How many bonds exists between two nitrogen atoms in dinitrogen gas?
explainAnswer: Identify the molecular formula of dinitrogen gas, which is N2.
Recall that nitrogen atoms have five valence electrons each.
Determine that to achieve a stable octet, each nitrogen atom needs three additional electrons.
Recognize that each shared pair of electrons forms a covalent bond, leading to three shared pairs between the two nitrogen atoms.
Conclude that there are three bonds between the two nitrogen atoms in dinitrogen gas.

text: What hard silvery-grey metal is the 9th most common element in the Earth’s crust, has an atomic number of 22, and takes its name from the Titans?
explainAnswer: Identify the atomic number given in the question, which is 22.
Recall the periodic table and find the element with atomic number 22.
Verify that the element is a hard silvery-grey metal.
Check the etymology of the element's name to confirm it is derived from the Titans.

text: If calcium were to combine with bromine to form a neutral molecule, what is the least number of calcium and bromine atoms, respectively, that would be required?
explainAnswer: Identify the charge of calcium, which is +2 as it is an alkaline earth metal.
Determine the charge of bromine, which is -1 as it is a halogen.
To balance the charges and form a neutral compound, one calcium ion (+2) needs two bromine ions (-1 each).
Thus, the least number of calcium and bromine atoms required is 1 calcium and 2 bromine.

text: If the atomic weight of manganese is 55, how many kilograms of manganese, to the third decimal place will contain two moles of manganese atoms?
explainAnswer: Identify the atomic weight of manganese, which is given as 55 grams per mole.
Calculate the total mass for two moles by multiplying the atomic weight by the number of moles: 55 g/mol * 2 moles = 110 grams.
Convert grams to kilograms by dividing the total grams by 1000: 110 grams / 1000 = 0.110 kilograms.

text: Using proper chemical formulas, finish balancing the following equation: Ba(OH)<sub>2</sub> + 2HCl → what?
explainAnswer: Identify the reactants and products in the equation.
Count the number of each type of atom on both sides of the equation.
Adjust the coefficients to balance the number of atoms for each element on both sides.
Write the balanced equation with the correct chemical formulas for the products.

text: A decrease of 1 unit on the pH scale represents which of the following:
choices: a 10-fold increase in the hydrogen ion concentration
a 10-fold decrease in the hydrogen ion concentration
a 100-fold increase in the hydrogen ion concentration
a 100-fold decrease in the hydrogen ion concentration
explainAnswer: Understand that the pH scale is logarithmic, meaning each whole number change on the scale represents a tenfold change in hydrogen ion concentration.
Recognize that a decrease of 1 unit in pH indicates an increase in hydrogen ion concentration.
Apply the logarithmic relationship: a decrease of 1 pH unit corresponds to an increase of 10 times the hydrogen ion concentration.
Conclude that a decrease of 1 unit on the pH scale represents a 10-fold increase in hydrogen ion concentration.

text: A chemical change occurs when a substance:
explainAnswer: Understand that a chemical change involves a transformation that alters the substance's chemical identity.
Identify that gaining or losing electrons typically results in a change in the chemical structure of a substance.
Recognize that changing state, reaching boiling point, or grinding a substance does not change its chemical identity, but rather its physical state or form.
Conclude that the only option that represents a true chemical change is gaining or losing electrons.

text: Which of the following molecules contains the largest bond angle?
explainAnswer: Identify the molecular geometry of each molecule.

Determine the bond angles based on the geometry: sulfur hexafluoride has octahedral geometry (90°), water has bent geometry (104.5°), carbon dioxide has linear geometry (180°), and boron trifluoride has trigonal planar geometry (120°).
Compare the bond angles to find the largest one.
Conclude that carbon dioxide has the largest bond angle of 180°.

text: Which general type of material is added to a reaction in order to lower the activation energy, thus making it proceed faster?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of substances in chemical reactions.
Recall that some substances can lower the activation energy of a reaction.
Define the term used for substances that facilitate reactions without being consumed.
Conclude that the substance that lowers activation energy is called a catalyst.

text: Given the equation H<sub>2</sub> + Cl<sub>2</sub> 2HCl + heat, if the reaction were performed with fluorine instead of chlorine, how many moles of H<sub>2</sub> would be required to yield two moles of HF?
explainAnswer: Identify the balanced chemical equation for the reaction with fluorine: H2 + F2 -> 2HF.
Determine the stoichiometric ratio from the balanced equation, which shows that 1 mole of H2 produces 2 moles of HF.
Since you want to produce 2 moles of HF, calculate the moles of H2 needed using the ratio: 2 moles of HF require 1 mole of H2.
Conclude that you need 1 mole of H2 to yield 2 moles of HF.

text: Identify all of the following three reactions that are synthesis reactions: 1) Hydrogen gas plus bromine gas yield hydrobromic acid; 2) Calcium bromide plus chlorine gas yields calcium chloride and bromine; 3) Solid tin plus oxygen gas yields tin oxide.
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of a synthesis reaction, which is a reaction where two or more reactants combine to form a single product.
Analyze the first reaction: hydrogen gas and bromine gas combine to form hydrobromic acid, which is a single product, confirming it is a synthesis reaction.
Examine the second reaction: calcium bromide and chlorine gas yield calcium chloride and bromine, resulting in two products, thus it is not a synthesis reaction.
Evaluate the third reaction: solid tin and oxygen gas combine to form tin oxide, which is a single product, confirming it is a synthesis reaction.

text: What functional group is represented by –NH<sub>2</sub>?
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical structure represented by –NH2.
Recognize that –NH2 consists of a nitrogen atom bonded to two hydrogen atoms.
Recall that functional groups are specific groups of atoms that determine the characteristics of a compound.
Know that the –NH2 group is characteristic of amines in organic chemistry.
Conclude that the functional group represented by –NH2 is an amine.

text: Of the following 3 forms of radioactive decay, which one is the MOST penetrating in human tissue and which one is the LEAST penetrating, respectively: alpha; beta; gamma
explainAnswer: Understand the three types of radioactive decay: alpha, beta, and gamma.
Recognize that alpha particles are heavy and positively charged, making them less penetrating and easily stopped by paper or skin.
Identify that beta particles are lighter and can penetrate further than alpha particles but are still stopped by materials like plastic or aluminum.
Know that gamma rays are electromagnetic radiation, which have no mass or charge, allowing them to penetrate deeply into materials, including human tissue.
Conclude that gamma is the most penetrating and alpha is the least penetrating.

text: What is the general term for compounds used in titrations that react with acids or bases to produce a color change?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which is about titrations in chemistry.
Recall that titrations involve the reaction of acids and bases.
Consider the role of substances that signal the endpoint of a titration.
Recognize that these substances change color when reacting with acids or bases.
Conclude that the general term for these substances is 'indicators'.

text: The time required for the Moon to return to the same position relative to the background stars (as seen from Earth) is about how long?
explainAnswer: Understand that the Moon's position relative to the stars changes due to both its orbit around Earth and Earth's orbit around the Sun.
Recognize that the Moon takes approximately 27.3 days to complete one orbit around Earth, known as the sidereal month.
Realize that the time it takes for the Moon to return to the same position relative to the Sun (and thus the background stars) is about 29.5 days, known as the synodic month.
Since a month is the closest option to the synodic month, choose 'A month' as the correct answer.

text: A substance with a pH of 2 has what pOH?
explainAnswer: Recall the relationship between pH and pOH, which is given by the equation pH + pOH = 14.
Substitute the given pH value of 2 into the equation: 2 + pOH = 14.
Solve for pOH by subtracting 2 from both sides: pOH = 14 - 2.
Calculate the result to find pOH = 12.

text: A piece of zinc is in a beaker of water. As you add hydrochloric acid to the beaker you see small gas bubbles forming around the zinc. What is this gas?
explainAnswer: Identify the reaction between zinc and hydrochloric acid, which produces a gas.
Recall that zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid to produce zinc chloride and hydrogen gas.
Recognize that the formation of bubbles indicates the release of a gas during the reaction.
Eliminate the other gas options based on the reaction context and properties.

text: Aside from carbon, which of the following elements can one find in Teflon?
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical composition of Teflon, which is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE).
Recognize that PTFE is made up of carbon (C) and fluorine (F) atoms.
Eliminate options that are not part of the chemical formula for Teflon, focusing on the given choices.
Confirm that fluorine is indeed present in Teflon, while the other elements (oxygen, chlorine, nitrogen) are not.

text: What color does copper burn in a flame?
explainAnswer: Recall the characteristic colors produced by different metal salts when burned in a flame.
Identify that copper compounds typically emit a green color when heated.
Confirm this by referencing reliable chemistry sources or flame test results.

text: What is the term for an insoluble product that is formed in a chemical reaction as a result of combining two liquids?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which involves a chemical reaction between two liquids.
Recall the definition of a precipitate, which is a solid that forms and separates from a liquid mixture.
Consider the conditions under which a precipitate is formed, such as mixing two solutions that react to create an insoluble compound.
Conclude that the term for the insoluble product formed in this scenario is 'precipitate'.

text: A blimp or airship that uses helium as its lifting gas primarily controls its buoyancy by doing which of the following:
choices: adding or removing small amounts of hydrogen gas because it is lighter than helium
heating or cooling the helium gas within the outside bladder of the blimp
explainAnswer: Understand that buoyancy in airships is controlled by the difference in density between the airship and the surrounding air.
Recognize that helium is already lighter than air, so the airship can adjust its overall density by changing the amount of air inside it.
Identify that intaking air increases the weight and decreases buoyancy, while venting air decreases the weight and increases buoyancy.
Eliminate other options by noting that helium is not produced or destroyed, and heating or cooling helium does not significantly change buoyancy compared to air intake or venting.

text: What is the term for the state at which the rate of the forward reaction is equal to the rate of the reverse reaction?
explainAnswer: Identify the concepts of forward and reverse reactions in a chemical context.
Understand that equilibrium occurs when the rates of these two reactions are equal.
Recall that at equilibrium, the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant over time.
Recognize that the term used to describe this state is 'equilibrium'.

text: Which of the following foods contains the MOST calories:
explainAnswer: Identify the calorie content of each food item provided in the choices.
Compare the calorie values of the twelve-ounce non-diet soda, 1 tablespoon catsup, 1 8-ounce fresh orange, and 1 tablespoon white granulated sugar.
Determine which food item has the highest calorie count based on the comparisons.
Conclude that the twelve-ounce non-diet soda contains the most calories.

text: Identify all of the following three mixtures that are considered heterogeneous mixtures: 1) Foam; 2) Alloy; 3) Air.
explainAnswer: Understand that a heterogeneous mixture is one where the components are not uniformly distributed and can be easily distinguished.
Analyze each option: Foam is made up of gas bubbles in a liquid, making it heterogeneous.
Recognize that an alloy is a homogeneous mixture of metals, and air is a homogeneous mixture of gases.
Conclude that only Foam meets the criteria for a heterogeneous mixture.

text: What isotope has nuclei [NEW-klee-eye] that contain six protons and seven neutrons?
explainAnswer: Identify the number of protons in the nucleus, which is given as six.
Determine the atomic number of the element, which corresponds to the number of protons; in this case, it is carbon (atomic number 6).
Count the number of neutrons provided, which is seven.
Calculate the mass number by adding the number of protons and neutrons together: 6 protons + 7 neutrons = 13.
Combine the element name with the mass number to identify the isotope as carbon-13.

text: The second electron shell in an atom can hold up to how many electrons, and contains how many different orbital shapes, respectively?
explainAnswer: Recall that the maximum number of electrons in a shell is given by the formula 2n^2, where n is the shell level.
For the second shell (n=2), calculate 2(2^2) which equals 8.
Identify that the second shell contains two types of orbitals: s and p.
Conclude that the second shell can hold 8 electrons and contains 2 different orbital shapes.

text: If the pH of a weak acid solution is equal to its pK a , what is the ratio of the concentrations of the acid and its conjugate base?
explainAnswer: Recall the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation, which relates pH, pK a, and the ratio of the concentrations of the acid and its conjugate base.
Recognize that when pH equals pK a, the equation simplifies to pH = pK a = log([A-]/[HA]).
Since the logarithm of a ratio equals zero when the ratio is 1, conclude that [A-]/[HA] = 1.
Thus, the concentrations of the acid and its conjugate base are equal.

text: What subatomic particles can be found in a cloud around the nucleus?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of an atom, which include protons, neutrons, and electrons.
Recognize that protons and neutrons are located in the nucleus of the atom.
Understand that electrons are the subatomic particles that exist in a cloud around the nucleus.
Conclude that the correct answer is electrons, as they are the only subatomic particles found in that region.

text: A new chemical is produced that is slippery and has a bitter taste but is not very corrosive. What is the most likely pH of this chemical?
explainAnswer: Identify that a slippery texture and bitter taste are characteristic of bases.
Recall that bases typically have a pH greater than 7.
Eliminate the options below 7, which are 3 and 7.
Consider that a pH of 9 indicates a weak base, which aligns with the description of being not very corrosive.
Select 9 as the most likely pH for the chemical.

text: What uranium isotope is most common on Earth?
explainAnswer: Identify the isotopes of uranium, which include uranium-234, uranium-235, and uranium-238.
Research the abundance of each isotope in nature.
Determine which isotope has the highest natural abundance.
Conclude that uranium-238 is the most common isotope found on Earth.

text: Which of the following substances when pure typically contains ONLY carbon atoms:
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical composition of each substance listed in the choices.
Determine which substances are made up of more than one type of atom.
Recognize that graphite is a form of carbon that consists solely of carbon atoms.
Conclude that graphite is the only substance listed that contains only carbon atoms.

text: What is the vertical distance from the undisturbed position of the medium to the top of a crest of a wave called?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms related to wave properties.
Understand that the undisturbed position of the medium is the equilibrium position.
Recognize that the distance from this position to the crest is a measure of energy in the wave.
Define this distance as the amplitude of the wave.

text: What chemical compound makes up the genetic material found inside of the nucleus?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of the cell nucleus.
Recall the role of genetic material in heredity.
Recognize that the primary genetic material in eukaryotic cells is DNA.
Specify the type of DNA that is found in the nucleus, which is deoxyribonucleic acid.

text: If an isotope undergoes first-order radioactive decay with a half-life of 5 years, how long will it take, in years, until only 12.5% of the isotope remains?
explainAnswer: Identify that a first-order radioactive decay means the amount of substance decreases by half every half-life.
Calculate how many half-lives it takes for the substance to reduce to 12.5% by recognizing that 12.5% is equivalent to 1/8 of the original amount.
Determine that 1/8 is equal to 2^-3, meaning it takes 3 half-lives to reach this amount.
Multiply the number of half-lives (3) by the duration of each half-life (5 years) to find the total time.
Conclude that 3 half-lives of 5 years each equals 15 years.

text: Identify all of the following three molecules that are diatomic: 1) Chlorine; 2) Water; 3) Hydrochloric acid.
explainAnswer: Recall that diatomic molecules consist of two atoms of the same or different elements.
Identify the chemical formula for each molecule: Chlorine (Cl2), Water (H2O), Hydrochloric acid (HCl).
Determine if each molecule is diatomic: Chlorine is diatomic (Cl2), Water is not (H2O), Hydrochloric acid is diatomic (HCl).
List the diatomic molecules identified: Chlorine and Hydrochloric acid.

text: What state of matter is responsible for the production of light in fluorescent and neon lights?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of states of matter: solid, liquid, gas, and plasma.
Understand that fluorescent and neon lights operate by exciting gas particles.
Recognize that when gas is ionized, it becomes plasma.
Conclude that plasma is the state of matter responsible for producing light in these types of lights.

text: Which of the following transformations is NOT a chemical change?
choices: Mixing solutions of magnesium sulfate and barium nitrate
Heating calcium carbonate until it expels a gas
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of a chemical change, which typically involves a change in composition or the formation of new substances.
Evaluate each option to determine if it results in a new substance or just a physical change.
Recognize that dissolving salt in water, mixing magnesium sulfate and barium nitrate, and heating calcium carbonate all involve chemical changes.
Note that vaporizing ethanol is a physical change, as it only changes the state of the substance without altering its chemical composition.

text: If an atom of neutral nitrogen has 7 protons, how many electrons will it have?
explainAnswer: Identify that a neutral atom has an equal number of protons and electrons.
Note that nitrogen has 7 protons.
Conclude that a neutral nitrogen atom must also have 7 electrons.

text: In the reaction sodium plus fluorine yields sodium fluoride, what are the reactants and products, respectively?
answer: REACTANTS = SODIUM AND FLUORINE; PRODUCTS = SODIUM FLUORIDE
explainAnswer: Identify the substances involved in the reaction, which are the starting materials known as reactants.
Recognize that sodium and fluorine are the elements that combine in this reaction.
Determine the outcome of the reaction, which is the compound formed, known as the product.
Conclude that sodium fluoride is the product formed from the combination of sodium and fluorine.

text: Nitrogen dioxide gas reacts with fluorine gas to form nitryl fluoride, FNO<sub>2</sub>. What is the sum of the coefficients of this balanced chemical reaction?
explainAnswer: Write the unbalanced chemical equation: NO2 + F2 -> FNO2.
Balance the nitrogen atoms by ensuring there is one nitrogen atom on each side.
Balance the fluorine atoms by adjusting the coefficients to have two fluorine atoms on the reactant side and one on the product side.
Balance the oxygen atoms by ensuring there are two oxygen atoms on the product side.
Count the coefficients in the balanced equation to find their sum.

text: Chlorine has an atomic mass of 35.45. Rank the following three chlorine isotopes in increasing order of their natural abundance: 1) Chlorine-35; 2) Chlorine-37; 3) Chlorine-38.
explainAnswer: Understand that the atomic mass of chlorine (35.45) indicates that the lighter isotope, Chlorine-35, is more abundant than the heavier isotopes.
Recognize that Chlorine-37 is the next most abundant isotope, as it contributes to the average atomic mass being closer to 35.45.
Identify that Chlorine-38 is the least abundant isotope since it is heavier and contributes less to the average atomic mass.
Rank the isotopes based on their abundance: Chlorine-38 (3), Chlorine-37 (2), Chlorine-35 (1).

text: How many protons does the heaviest isotope of hydrogen have?
explainAnswer: Identify the element in question, which is hydrogen.
Determine the definition of an isotope, which is a variant of an element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Recognize that all isotopes of hydrogen, including the heaviest one (deuterium or tritium), still have 1 proton.
Conclude that the number of protons in the heaviest isotope of hydrogen is 1.

text: What is the term for the energy required to start a chemical reaction and form the transition state?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept related to chemical reactions and energy.
Recall the definition of the energy needed to initiate a reaction.
Recognize that this energy is associated with reaching the transition state.
Conclude that the term for this energy is activation energy.

text: Identify all of the following four elements that are naturally diatomic or polyatomic elements: 1) nitrogen, 2) silicon, 3) phosphorous, 4) selenium.
explainAnswer: Recall that diatomic elements exist as pairs of atoms, while polyatomic elements consist of three or more atoms.
Identify the common naturally diatomic elements, which include nitrogen (N2) and others like oxygen and hydrogen.
Recognize that phosphorus (P4) and selenium (Se8) are examples of polyatomic elements.
Eliminate silicon (Si) from the list as it is not diatomic or polyatomic in its natural state.

text: Which of the following would be the most accurate glassware to use to measure a volume of water?
explainAnswer: Identify the purpose of the glassware options provided.
Consider the accuracy and precision of each type of glassware.
Determine which glassware is designed specifically for measuring volumes accurately.
Select the graduated cylinder as it has clear markings for precise volume measurement.

text: The atomic number of molybdenum is 42. What does this number indicate?
choices: Every atom has 42 total protons & neutrons in the nucleus
Every atom has a mass of 42 a.m.u.
Every atom has 42 protons in the nucleus
Every atom will form bonds that measure 42 degrees
explainAnswer: Identify what the atomic number represents in an element.
Recall that the atomic number is defined as the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
Eliminate the incorrect choices based on the definition of atomic number.
Select the correct answer that states every atom has 42 protons in the nucleus.

text: What is the name for the procedure which is used to separate molecules of different polarity by placing them on paper and then placing the bottom edge of the paper on in a certain polar or nonpolar solvent?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in the question, such as 'separate molecules', 'polarity', and 'paper'.
Recall the common laboratory techniques used for separating substances based on their properties.
Eliminate the options that do not relate to the separation of molecules by polarity.
Recognize that chromatography specifically involves the use of a solvent and a stationary phase, like paper, to separate compounds.
Conclude that the correct answer is chromatography.

text: Which of the following is NOT an acid-base conjugate pair?
explainAnswer: Identify what an acid-base conjugate pair is: a pair of species that differ by a proton (H+).
Examine each choice to see if they fit the definition of an acid-base conjugate pair.
For H3O+ and H2O, H3O+ donates a proton to form H2O, so they are a conjugate pair.
For NH4+ and NH3, NH4+ donates a proton to form NH3, making them a conjugate pair as well.
For H2SO4 and OH−, H2SO4 does not donate a proton to form OH−, so they are not a conjugate pair.

text: One liter of oxygen and two liters of hydrogen are reacted in a closed container to form a gaseous product. If the temperature within the container is the same before and after the reaction, what is the ratio of final pressure to initial pressure in the container?
explainAnswer: Identify the initial amounts of gases: 1 liter of oxygen (O2) and 2 liters of hydrogen (H2).
Determine the balanced chemical equation for the reaction: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O.
Calculate the total initial volume of gases: 1 liter (O2) + 2 liters (H2) = 3 liters.
After the reaction, water vapor is produced, which occupies a smaller volume than the original gases; thus, the final volume is less than 3 liters.
Use the ideal gas law to find the ratio of final pressure to initial pressure, which results in a ratio of 2:3.

text: What is the common name of the acid HClO<sub>2</sub>?
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical formula HClO2 and recognize that it contains chlorine, hydrogen, and oxygen.
Determine the oxidation state of chlorine in HClO2, which is +3.
Recall that acids derived from oxyanions typically have names based on the anion; HClO2 corresponds to the chlorite ion (ClO2-).
Use the naming convention for acids: the acid derived from the chlorite ion is called chlorous acid.

text: Giving your answer in scientific notation to the second decimal place, how many molecules are in 10 moles of H<sub>2</sub>O?
explainAnswer: Identify that 1 mole of any substance contains Avogadro's number of molecules, which is approximately 6.02 × 10^23.
Multiply the number of moles (10) by Avogadro's number (6.02 × 10^23) to find the total number of molecules.
Express the result in scientific notation, ensuring it is to the second decimal place.

text: Lithium is well-suited for use in lightweight batteries for fuel- efficient transportation like electric cars and aircraft such as the 787 Dreamliner because of its low atomic mass. Atoms of what two elements are less massive than lithium?
explainAnswer: Identify the atomic mass of lithium, which is approximately 6.94 u.
Consult the periodic table to find elements with atomic masses less than 6.94 u.
Look for the atomic masses of hydrogen (approximately 1.01 u) and helium (approximately 4.00 u).
Confirm that both hydrogen and helium have atomic masses less than that of lithium.

text: In high-density polyethylene, or HDPE, each carbon atom bonds to how many other carbon atoms?
explainAnswer: Identify the structure of high-density polyethylene (HDPE) as a polymer made of repeating units of ethylene.
Recognize that each ethylene unit consists of two carbon atoms bonded to each other.
Understand that in HDPE, each carbon atom in the chain is bonded to two neighboring carbon atoms.
Conclude that each carbon atom in HDPE bonds to 2 other carbon atoms.

text: Name the process during which nuclear energy is released when the nuclei of hydrogen atoms are combined to form helium.
explainAnswer: Identify the type of nuclear reaction that involves combining lighter atomic nuclei.
Recall that the process of combining hydrogen nuclei typically results in the formation of helium.
Recognize that this process releases a significant amount of energy.
Conclude that the correct term for this process is fusion or nuclear fusion.

text: Which of the following solutions will conduct electricity the best?
explainAnswer: Identify that electrical conductivity in solutions is due to the presence of ions.
Evaluate each option to see if it contains ionic compounds that dissociate in water.
Recognize that sodium chloride (NaCl) dissociates into sodium (Na+) and chloride (Cl-) ions in water.
Compare the ionic dissociation of sodium chloride with the other options, which do not produce ions.
Conclude that sodium chloride and distilled water will conduct electricity the best due to the presence of free ions.

text: Which of the following processes is exothermic:
choices: solid water changes to water vapor
solid water changes to liquid water
liquid water changes to solid water
liquid water changes to water vapor
explainAnswer: Understand that an exothermic process releases heat to the surroundings.
Identify the phase changes listed in the choices and determine their energy changes.
Recognize that freezing (liquid to solid) releases energy, making it exothermic.
Eliminate the other options as they either absorb heat or do not release it.

text: Which of the following is NOT true about solutions:
choices: ethylene glycol, or antifreeze, lowers the freezing point of water in a car radiator
reverse osmosis is used to convert salt water into fresh water
the presence of colloidal particles in solution is easily detected by a beam of light
a solution of hydrochloric acid acts as an ideal proton acceptor
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of solutions mentioned in each choice.
Evaluate the role of hydrochloric acid in terms of proton donation and acceptance.
Determine which statement contradicts the established properties of acids and bases.
Conclude that hydrochloric acid is a strong acid that donates protons, not accepts them.

text: A student is spinning a yo-yo in a vertical loop. When the yo-yo is at the top of the loop, in what direction is the acceleration vector of the yo-yo pointing?
explainAnswer: Identify that the yo-yo is in a vertical loop and consider the forces acting on it at the top of the loop.
Recognize that at the top of the loop, gravity acts downward on the yo-yo.
Understand that for an object in circular motion, the net acceleration must point towards the center of the circular path.
Since the center of the loop is below the yo-yo when it is at the top, the acceleration vector must also point downward.

text: Magnetic fields such as those exhibited by permanent magnets, are created via the motion of what subatomic particle?
explainAnswer: Identify the subatomic particles that can create magnetic fields, focusing on electrons, protons, and neutrons.
Understand that magnetic fields are primarily produced by the motion of charged particles.
Recognize that electrons are the subatomic particles that move and generate magnetic fields in materials.
Conclude that since electrons are responsible for creating magnetic fields, the correct answer is 'electron'.

text: A scientist dissolves 1 mole of a certain acid in 100 grams of water at 25 degrees Celsius and finds that the temperature increases by 7 degrees. In kilojoules per mole to two significant figures, what is the enthalpy of dissolution of the acid?
explainAnswer: Calculate the mass of water in kilograms by dividing 100 grams by 1000.
Use the specific heat capacity of water (4.18 J/g°C) to calculate the heat absorbed by the water using the formula q = mass × specific heat × temperature change.
Convert the heat absorbed from joules to kilojoules by dividing by 1000.
Since the enthalpy of dissolution is per mole, divide the total heat absorbed by the number of moles of acid (1 mole) to find the enthalpy of dissolution.
Express the final answer in kilojoules per mole and round to two significant figures, ensuring to include the negative sign for exothermic dissolution.

text: The particles of which of the following states of matter have the strongest attraction between them?
explainAnswer: Identify the states of matter: gas, liquid, plasma, and solid.
Recall that in solids, particles are closely packed together and vibrate in fixed positions.
Compare the arrangement and movement of particles in each state: gases have weak attractions, liquids have moderate attractions, and solids have strong attractions.
Conclude that solids have the strongest attractions between particles due to their fixed positions and close proximity.

text: Which of the following is closest to the diameter, in meters, of the nucleus of a zinc atom?
explainAnswer: Recall that the diameter of an atomic nucleus is typically on the order of 10<sup>–14</sup> meters.
Consider that the nucleus is much smaller than the overall size of the atom, which is about 10<sup>–10</sup> meters.
Review the typical sizes of nuclei for various elements, noting that they generally fall within the range of 10<sup>–14</sup> meters.
Eliminate the other options based on their size being too large compared to typical nuclear diameters.

text: Which of the following is NOT a hazard that would be listed on the Material Safety Data Sheet for concentrated sulfuric acid:
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of concentrated sulfuric acid.
Review the common hazards associated with sulfuric acid, such as corrosiveness and toxicity.
Determine which of the listed options is not typically associated with sulfuric acid.
Conclude that 'flammable' is the correct answer, as sulfuric acid is not classified as flammable.

text: What type of reaction is Na<sub>2</sub>S + 2HCl yields 2NaCl + H<sub>2</sub>S an example of?
explainAnswer: Identify the reactants and products in the reaction.
Look for the exchange of ions between the reactants.
Determine if the reaction involves two compounds reacting to form two new compounds.
Confirm that the reaction fits the definition of a double replacement reaction.

text: If a solution has a low pH, what ion predominates in the solution?
explainAnswer: Recall that pH is a measure of the hydrogen ion concentration in a solution.
Understand that a low pH indicates a high concentration of hydrogen ions.
Recognize that in aqueous solutions, hydrogen ions (H+) associate with water molecules to form hydronium ions (H3O+).
Conclude that in a solution with low pH, hydronium ions predominate.

text: Which of the following describes most of the elements on the periodic table?
explainAnswer: Identify the categories of elements on the periodic table.
Determine the properties associated with each category.
Evaluate which category includes the majority of elements based on their properties.
Conclude that conductors, primarily metals, make up most of the periodic table.

text: What is the force that opposes the motion of an object?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which is about forces acting on objects.
Recall the types of forces that can oppose motion, such as friction, air resistance, and tension.
Focus on the force that specifically acts to resist the sliding or rolling of surfaces against each other.
Conclude that the force that opposes the motion of an object is known as friction.

text: What type of energy is associated with an object's motion?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of energy related to motion.
Recall the definition of kinetic energy.
Understand that kinetic energy is the energy an object possesses due to its velocity.
Conclude that the type of energy associated with an object's motion is kinetic energy.

text: What acid is produced when carbon dioxide reacts with water during carbon sequestration?
explainAnswer: Identify the reactants involved in the reaction, which are carbon dioxide (CO2) and water (H2O).
Recognize that when CO2 dissolves in water, it undergoes a chemical reaction.
Recall the chemical equation for this reaction, which produces carbonic acid (H2CO3).
Conclude that the product of the reaction is carbonic acid.

text: What is the molar volume, to the nearest tenth of a liter, of an ideal gas at standard pressure?
explainAnswer: Understand that the molar volume of an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure (STP) is a defined value.
Recall that STP is defined as 0 degrees Celsius (273.15 K) and 1 atmosphere (atm) of pressure.
Use the known value that at STP, one mole of an ideal gas occupies 22.4 liters.
Round the value to the nearest tenth if necessary, but in this case, it remains 22.4 liters.

text: A boy holds a 5-kilogram weight in position on a shelf to prevent it from falling. After 10 minutes, how much work, in joules, did he perform on the weight?
explainAnswer: Identify that work is defined as force applied over a distance.
Recognize that the boy is holding the weight stationary, meaning there is no movement.
Since there is no distance moved, the work done is zero.
Conclude that the work performed on the weight is 0 joules.

text: What type of bonds are the main intermolecular forces that allow water molecules to undergo cohesion?
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of water that contribute to cohesion.
Recall the types of intermolecular forces present in substances.
Determine which intermolecular force is specifically responsible for the unique properties of water.
Conclude that hydrogen bonds are the primary intermolecular forces that enable cohesion in water.

text: Rank the following three atoms in terms of increasing number of valence electrons: 1) Carbon; 2) Beryllium; 3) Fluorine.
explainAnswer: Identify the atomic number of each element: Carbon (6), Beryllium (4), Fluorine (9).
Determine the number of valence electrons for each element: Carbon has 4, Beryllium has 2, and Fluorine has 7.
Rank the elements based on their valence electrons from lowest to highest: Beryllium (2), Carbon (4), Fluorine (7).
Conclude the ranking as Beryllium (2), Carbon (1), Fluorine (3).

text: Given that you have one mole of each of the following three substances at 4 degrees Celsius, rank them in terms of increasing temperature change when 100 calories of energy is transferred into them: 1) Copper; 2) Nitrogen gas kept at constant volume; 3) Borosilicate glass.
explainAnswer: Identify the specific heat capacities of copper, borosilicate glass, and nitrogen gas at constant volume.
Calculate the temperature change for each substance using the formula: temperature change = energy transferred / (mass * specific heat capacity).
Rank the calculated temperature changes from smallest to largest.
Determine that copper has the highest specific heat capacity, followed by borosilicate glass, and nitrogen gas has the lowest specific heat capacity, leading to the final ranking.

text: Order the following four elements from least electronegative to most electronegative: 1) carbon; 2) oxygen; 3) nitrogen; 4) fluorine.
explainAnswer: Recall the electronegativity values of the elements: carbon (2.5), nitrogen (3.0), oxygen (3.5), and fluorine (4.0).
List the elements in order of their electronegativity values from lowest to highest.
Identify the order as carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and fluorine.

text: Identify all of the following four choices that are electrically neutral: 1) gamma rays, 2) positrons, 3) alpha particles, 4) beta particles.
explainAnswer: Understand that electrically neutral particles have no net charge.
Identify that gamma rays are electromagnetic radiation and carry no charge.
Recognize that positrons are positively charged particles, while beta particles (electrons) are negatively charged.
Note that alpha particles consist of two protons and two neutrons, giving them a positive charge.
Conclude that only gamma rays are electrically neutral among the given choices.

text: Which of the following elements is NOT a metalloid?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of metalloids, which are elements that have properties of both metals and nonmetals.
List the elements provided: Silicon, Germanium, Carbon, Tellurium.
Determine which of these elements are classified as metalloids: Silicon, Germanium, and Tellurium are metalloids.
Recognize that Carbon is a nonmetal, thus it does not fit the definition of a metalloid.
Conclude that Carbon is the element that is NOT a metalloid.

text: When aluminum filings are added to a beaker containing concentrated sulfuric acid, what gas is produced?
explainAnswer: Identify the reaction between aluminum and sulfuric acid.
Recognize that aluminum reacts with acids to produce hydrogen gas.
Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction.
Conclude that hydrogen gas is the product of this reaction.

text: Which of the following foods contains the MOST grams of carbohydrates:
explainAnswer: Identify the carbohydrate content of each food item.
Research or recall the average carbohydrate grams for 3 ounces of fried beef liver, 1 cup of lard, 1 cup of white granulated sugar, and 1 baked potato.
Compare the carbohydrate amounts to determine which food has the highest content.
Conclude that 1 cup of white granulated sugar contains the most grams of carbohydrates.

text: Which of the following is the greatest contributor to ambient carbon monoxide concentrations in the U.S.:
explainAnswer: Identify the sources of carbon monoxide emissions listed in the choices.
Research or recall data on carbon monoxide emissions by source in the U.S.
Compare the contributions of each source to determine which has the highest level.
Conclude that transportation is the greatest contributor based on the data reviewed.

text: Which of the following is true of tension?
choices: It is the same as stress
Its magnitude is independent of mass
It can be defined as the opposite of compression
explainAnswer: Understand the definitions of tension and compression in physics.
Identify that tension refers to the pulling force exerted by a string, rope, or cable.
Recognize that compression refers to the pushing force that shortens an object.
Determine that tension is indeed the opposite of compression, as it involves pulling rather than pushing.
Eliminate the other choices based on their definitions and relationships to tension.

text: Identify all of the following three molecules that are examples of alkenes: 1) Propene; 2) Cyclopropene; 3) Cyclohexane.
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of an alkene, which is a hydrocarbon containing at least one carbon-carbon double bond.
Examine each molecule to determine if it contains a carbon-carbon double bond.
Propene has a double bond between two carbon atoms, confirming it is an alkene.
Cyclopropene also has a double bond in its ring structure, confirming it is an alkene.
Cyclohexane has only single bonds between carbon atoms, so it is not an alkene.

text: With respect to atomic orbitals, what is the maximum number of electrons in the second energy level?
explainAnswer: Identify the energy level in question, which is the second energy level (n=2).
Recall that the maximum number of electrons in an energy level is given by the formula 2n^2.
Substitute n=2 into the formula: 2(2^2) = 2(4).
Calculate the result: 2(4) = 8.
Conclude that the maximum number of electrons in the second energy level is 8.

text: What is the most common scientific term for the chemical reaction in which oxygen combines with a substance or hydrogens are removed from a substance?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of chemical reaction described in the question.
Recognize that the reaction involves oxygen combining with another substance.
Understand that this process often involves the removal of electrons or hydrogen.
Recall the scientific term that describes this process, which is oxidation.

text: According to alkane nomenclature, the two in 2-methylpentane indicates the position of what functional group?
explainAnswer: Identify the main chain of the alkane, which in this case is pentane.
Determine the substituent group attached to the main chain, which is a methyl group.
Recognize that the '2' in 2-methylpentane indicates the position of the methyl group on the second carbon of the main chain.

text: Which of the following is a water-purification process that uses pressure across a semi-permeable membrane:
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in the question, specifically 'water-purification process' and 'semi-permeable membrane'.
Review the provided choices to determine which method involves pressure and a semi-permeable membrane.
Recognize that reverse osmosis is a known process that fits both criteria of using pressure and a semi-permeable membrane.
Eliminate the other options based on their definitions and methods of operation.
Conclude that reverse osmosis is the correct answer.

text: Given the combustion equation 2C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub> + 13O<sub>2</sub> → 8CO<sub>2</sub> + 10H<sub>2</sub>O, how many moles of water can be produced by reacting 12.5 moles of C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub> with excess oxygen?
explainAnswer: Identify the mole ratio of C4H10 to H2O from the balanced equation, which is 2 moles of C4H10 producing 10 moles of H2O.
Calculate the number of moles of H2O produced per mole of C4H10 by dividing 10 by 2, which equals 5 moles of H2O per mole of C4H10.
Multiply the number of moles of C4H10 (12.5 moles) by the moles of H2O produced per mole of C4H10 (5 moles).
Perform the multiplication: 12.5 moles of C4H10 times 5 moles of H2O equals 62.5 moles of H2O.

text: An atom’s ability to react with other atoms is determined by what type of subatomic particle?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of each subatomic particle in an atom.
Understand that protons and neutrons are located in the nucleus and do not participate in chemical reactions.
Recognize that electrons are found in the outer shells and are involved in bonding and reactions with other atoms.
Conclude that the ability of an atom to react is primarily determined by its electrons.

text: Calculate the volume in milliliters of a solution necessary to make 2 liters of a 1 millimolar solution from a 0.1 molar solution.
explainAnswer: Convert 2 liters to milliliters, which is 2000 mL.
Determine the total number of moles needed for a 1 millimolar solution in 2000 mL, which is 0.002 moles.
Calculate the volume of the 0.1 molar solution needed to obtain 0.002 moles using the formula: Volume (L) = Moles / Molarity.
Substituting the values gives Volume = 0.002 moles / 0.1 M = 0.02 L.
Convert 0.02 L to milliliters, which is 20 mL.

text: Which of the following elements can form a monatomic gas at standard temperature and pressure?
explainAnswer: Identify the elements listed in the choices.
Determine the state of each element at standard temperature and pressure (STP).
Recall that monatomic gases are typically noble gases.
Recognize that Neon is a noble gas and exists as a monatomic gas at STP.
Conclude that Neon is the only element from the choices that forms a monatomic gas at STP.

text: If the half-life of a given isotope is 7 days, what fraction of the original isotope will be left after 14 days?
explainAnswer: Identify the half-life of the isotope, which is 7 days.
Determine how many half-lives fit into 14 days by dividing 14 by 7, resulting in 2 half-lives.
Calculate the remaining fraction of the isotope after each half-life: after the first half-life, 1/2 remains, and after the second half-life, 1/2 of 1/2 remains, which is 1/4.
Conclude that the fraction of the original isotope left after 14 days is 1/4.

text: What is the empirical formula of ammonium sulfate?
explainAnswer: Identify the constituent elements in ammonium sulfate, which are nitrogen (N), hydrogen (H), and sulfur (S), along with oxygen (O).
Determine the number of each type of atom in the compound: ammonium (NH4) has 1 nitrogen and 4 hydrogens, and sulfate (SO4) has 1 sulfur and 4 oxygens.
Combine the counts of each atom to form the empirical formula: there is 1 nitrogen, 4 hydrogens, 1 sulfur, and 4 oxygens.
Write the empirical formula by listing the elements with their respective counts: NH4 for ammonium and SO4 for sulfate, resulting in (NH4)2SO4 as the full formula for ammonium sulfate.

text: A student is preparing 500 milliliters of a 6-millimolar solution of copper (II) sulfate. Which of the following pieces of glassware would be best for the most precise measurement of 500 milliliters of this solution?
explainAnswer: Identify the requirement for precise measurement of a specific volume of solution.
Evaluate the options given for their precision in measuring liquid volumes.
Determine that a volumetric flask is designed for accurate measurement of a single volume.
Conclude that the volumetric flask is the best choice for preparing a 500 milliliter solution.

text: The particles in an atom that determine which element it is are the:
explainAnswer: Identify the role of each type of particle in an atom: protons, neutrons, and electrons.
Understand that protons determine the atomic number of an element.
Recall that the atomic number defines the identity of an element.
Conclude that the correct answer is protons, as they uniquely identify the element.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of water solubility: 1) Increasing the temperature increases solubility of sugar; 2) Increasing the temperature increases the rate of dissolving of sugar; 3) Increasing the temperature increases the solubility of calcium carbonate.
explainAnswer: Evaluate the effect of temperature on the solubility of sugar, noting that it generally increases with temperature.
Consider the rate of dissolving for sugar, which also tends to increase with higher temperatures due to increased molecular movement.
Research the solubility of calcium carbonate in water, which typically decreases with increasing temperature, indicating that statement 3 is false.

text: The reaction of hydrocarbons found in such things as wood and paper with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide, water and heat is called:
explainAnswer: Identify the key components of the reaction described: hydrocarbons, oxygen, carbon dioxide, water, and heat.
Recall the definitions of the provided choices: fission, fusion, endothermic, and combustion.
Recognize that the reaction involving hydrocarbons and oxygen producing carbon dioxide and water is a common characteristic of combustion.
Eliminate the other options as they do not fit the description of the reaction involving heat release.

text: Which of the following elements is the most electronegative?
explainAnswer: Recall the concept of electronegativity, which is the tendency of an atom to attract electrons in a bond.
Refer to the periodic table to identify the position of each element: Sodium (Na) is in group 1, Boron (B) is in group 13, Carbon (C) is in group 14, and Rubidium (Rb) is in group 1.
Note that electronegativity generally increases across a period (left to right) and decreases down a group (top to bottom).

Compare the elements: Sodium and Rubidium are both in group 1 and have low electronegativity, Boron has moderate electronegativity, while Carbon, being further right in the same period as Boron, has higher electronegativity.
Conclude that Carbon is the most electronegative element among the given choices.

text: The maximum amount of elemental barium allowed in drinking water by the EPA is 2 milligrams per liter. Barium has an atomic mass of 140 grams per mole. In millimoles and to two significant figures, what is the maximum amount of barium allowed in one liter of drinking water?
explainAnswer: Convert the maximum amount of barium from milligrams to grams by dividing by 1000, which gives 0.002 grams.
Use the atomic mass of barium (140 grams per mole) to find the number of moles by dividing the mass in grams by the atomic mass: 0.002 grams / 140 grams per mole.
Convert the number of moles to millimoles by multiplying by 1000, since 1 mole equals 1000 millimoles.
Round the final answer to two significant figures.

text: What is the name given to the superposition of two or more waves resulting in a new wave pattern?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of wave behavior in physics.
Recall the principle of superposition, which states that when two or more waves overlap, they combine to form a new wave.
Recognize that the resulting wave pattern from this combination is known as interference.
Differentiate between constructive and destructive interference as types of wave interactions.

text: An atom of radon-222 loses an alpha particle to become a more stable atom of which of the following?
explainAnswer: Identify that an alpha particle consists of 2 protons and 2 neutrons.
Determine the atomic number of radon-222, which is 86.
Subtract 2 from the atomic number of radon to find the atomic number of the new element after alpha decay, which is 84.
Consult the periodic table to find that the element with atomic number 84 is polonium.

text: Which of the following is the best strategy to compensate for random errors during an experiment in an unbiased manner?
choices: Using machine learning to model error
Apply a filter to reduce noise
explainAnswer: Identify the nature of random errors in experiments, which are unpredictable fluctuations in measurements.
Evaluate the options provided to determine which method can effectively reduce the impact of these random errors.
Recognize that making repeated independent measurements allows for averaging out the random fluctuations.
Conclude that this method provides a more reliable estimate of the true value, thus compensating for random errors in an unbiased manner.

text: A chemistry experiment calls for 10.0 liters of a 0.8 molar solution of a chemical with a molecular weight of 100 grams per mole. How many grams of the chemical will you need to weigh out to make this solution?
explainAnswer: Calculate the number of moles needed by multiplying the volume of the solution (10.0 liters) by the molarity (0.8 moles/liter).
This gives you 8.0 moles of the chemical (10.0 L * 0.8 mol/L = 8.0 moles).
Next, multiply the number of moles (8.0 moles) by the molecular weight of the chemical (100 grams/mole).
This results in 800 grams of the chemical needed (8.0 moles * 100 g/mole = 800 grams).

text: Which of the following solutions will conduct electricity the best?
explainAnswer: Identify the substances in each solution and their ability to dissociate into ions.
Recognize that sodium chloride (NaCl) dissociates into Na+ and Cl- ions in water, making it an electrolyte.
Understand that sugar, alcohol, and moth balls do not dissociate into ions in solution, thus they do not conduct electricity well.
Compare the conductivity of the solutions based on the presence of ions, concluding that sodium chloride and distilled water will conduct electricity the best.

text: For a given compound, motion at the molecular level is:
explainAnswer: Understand that molecular motion varies by state of matter: solid, liquid, and gas.
Recognize that in solids, molecules are tightly packed and vibrate in place.
Note that in liquids, molecules are more loosely packed and can slide past each other, allowing for some motion.
Identify that in gases, molecules are far apart and move freely and rapidly in all directions.
Conclude that since gas molecules have the most freedom of movement, their motion is greatest compared to solids and liquids.

text: Which of the following is NOT true regarding radioactive decay?
choices: In gamma decay, no transmutation occurs
Different isotopes of the same element will decay at the same rate
Radioactive decay may cause an atom to lose protons or neutrons
Radioactive decay is a process by which unstable atoms emit ionizing particles
explainAnswer: Identify the key concepts related to radioactive decay and its types.
Evaluate each statement to determine its truthfulness based on the principles of radioactive decay.
Focus on the statement about different isotopes decaying at the same rate and compare it with known facts about isotopes.
Conclude that the statement about isotopes decaying at the same rate is false, as decay rates vary between different isotopes.

text: What kind of organic compound is formed by the reaction of an organic acid and an alcohol?
explainAnswer: Identify the reactants involved: an organic acid and an alcohol.
Recognize that the reaction between these two types of compounds is known as esterification.
Understand that the product of this reaction is an ester.
Recall the general structure of esters, which includes a carbonyl group and an alkoxy group.
Conclude that the compound formed is classified as an ester.

text: Which of the following increases with the addition of sodium chloride to water?
choices: The boiling point of the solution
The freezing point of the solution
The vapor pressure of the solution
explainAnswer: Understand that adding a solute like sodium chloride to water affects its physical properties.
Recognize that the boiling point elevation is a colligative property, which means it depends on the number of solute particles in the solution.
Identify that sodium chloride dissociates into sodium and chloride ions, increasing the number of solute particles.
Conclude that this increase in solute particles raises the boiling point of the solution.

text: What is the molecular formula for amazonite?
explainAnswer: Identify the elements present in amazonite, which are potassium (K), aluminum (Al), silicon (Si), and oxygen (O).
Determine the ratio of each element in the mineral's structure.
Combine the symbols of the elements with their respective ratios to form the molecular formula.
Since oxygen is not included in the final answer, focus on the remaining elements: K, Al, and Si.

text: An amine is characterized by what element that usually possesses a lone pair in compounds?
explainAnswer: Identify the functional groups associated with amines.
Recall that amines are derived from ammonia (NH3).
Recognize that nitrogen is the central atom in ammonia and amines.
Note that nitrogen typically has a lone pair of electrons in its compounds.

text: Alpha decay occurs when an atom emits an alpha particle. What is an alpha particle?
explainAnswer: Identify that an alpha particle is a type of nuclear radiation.
Recall the composition of an alpha particle, which consists of protons and neutrons.
Determine the specific numbers of protons and neutrons in an alpha particle, which are 2 protons and 2 neutrons.

text: What is the common name for the organic solvent which is the main ingredient in nail polish remover?
explainAnswer: Recall that nail polish remover is typically used to dissolve nail polish.
Identify the main chemical component commonly associated with nail polish remover.
Recognize that acetone is widely known as a solvent for this purpose.
Conclude that the common name for the organic solvent in nail polish remover is acetone.

text: Which of the following liquids at room temperature and 1 atmosphere would have the GREATEST surface tension:
explainAnswer: Understand that surface tension is a property of liquids that is influenced by the strength of intermolecular forces.

Identify the types of intermolecular forces present in each liquid: distilled water has hydrogen bonding, while ethanol, methanol, and acetone have weaker hydrogen bonding or dipole-dipole interactions.
Compare the strength of the intermolecular forces: hydrogen bonds in water are stronger than those in ethanol, methanol, and acetone.
Conclude that the liquid with the strongest intermolecular forces will have the greatest surface tension, which is distilled water.

text: Today we often hear of politicians being given the litmus test to determine their character. However, in science, what chemical property does a litmus test measure?
explainAnswer: Identify what a litmus test is used for in scientific contexts.
Understand that a litmus test involves using litmus paper that changes color in response to pH levels.
Recognize that the pH scale measures how acidic or basic a solution is.
Conclude that since the litmus test indicates pH, it measures acidity.

text: Which of the following best describes how a chemical change occurs in a substance?
choices: It gains, loses, or shares electrons
It is ground into a powder
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of physical and chemical changes.
Recognize that a chemical change involves the alteration of a substance's molecular structure.
Determine that gaining, losing, or sharing electrons indicates a change in chemical bonds.
Eliminate options that describe physical changes or states of matter rather than chemical interactions.

text: What is the smallest non-divisible unit of a covalent compound?
explainAnswer: Understand that covalent compounds are formed by the sharing of electrons between atoms.
Identify that the smallest unit of a covalent compound that retains its chemical properties is called a molecule.
Recognize that a molecule can consist of two or more atoms bonded together.
Conclude that the answer to the question is 'molecule' as it is the smallest non-divisible unit of a covalent compound.

text: Hydrocarbons that contain at least one double bond between carbon atoms are classified as which of the following?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of bonds present in hydrocarbons, focusing on single and double bonds.
Recall that hydrocarbons with only single bonds are classified as saturated.
Recognize that hydrocarbons with at least one double bond are classified as unsaturated.
Eliminate the other options based on their definitions, confirming that unsaturated is the correct classification.

text: Given a constant number of gas molecules, the ideal gas law describes the relationship between pressure, volume, and what other property?
explainAnswer: Identify the ideal gas law equation, which is PV = nRT.
Recognize that P is pressure, V is volume, n is the number of moles, R is the ideal gas constant, and T is temperature.
Understand that with a constant number of gas molecules (n), the relationship between pressure, volume, and temperature must hold true.
Conclude that temperature is the remaining property that relates to pressure and volume in the ideal gas law.

text: What aqueous acid primarily results from the production of acid rain?
explainAnswer: Identify the primary components of acid rain, which are typically sulfur dioxide (SO2) and nitrogen oxides (NOx).
Understand that sulfur dioxide is a major contributor to acid rain as it reacts with water in the atmosphere.
Recognize that sulfur dioxide is converted into sulfuric acid (H2SO4) when it reacts with water and oxygen.
Conclude that the primary aqueous acid resulting from this process is sulfuric acid.

text: Which of the following explains the size of a chloride ion compared to that of a chlorine atom?
choices: Chloride is smaller because it has fewer electrons
Chloride is smaller because it has more electrons
Chloride is larger because it has fewer electrons
Chloride is larger because it has more electrons
explainAnswer: Understand that a chloride ion (Cl-) is formed when a chlorine atom gains an electron.
Recognize that gaining an electron increases the electron-electron repulsion in the outer shell.
