Realize that this increased repulsion causes the electron cloud to expand, making the ion larger than the neutral atom.
Conclude that since chloride has more electrons than chlorine, it is larger.

text: What is the chemical name for the compound NaCl?
explainAnswer: Identify the elements present in the compound NaCl, which are sodium (Na) and chlorine (Cl).
Determine the common names of these elements, which are sodium for Na and chloride for Cl.
Combine the names of the elements, using 'sodium' for Na and 'chloride' for Cl, to form the chemical name.
The final chemical name for NaCl is sodium chloride.

text: Identify the following three elements as a metal, metalloid and nonmetal, respectively: silicon, sodium, neon.
answer: METAL = SODIUM; METALLOID = SILICON; NONMETAL = NEON
explainAnswer: Recall the periodic table classification of elements.
Identify sodium as a metal, which is typically found on the left side of the periodic table.
Recognize silicon as a metalloid, which has properties of both metals and nonmetals and is located along the zig-zag line.
Identify neon as a nonmetal, specifically a noble gas, which is found on the far right of the periodic table.

text: On the periodic table, what is the name of the group of elements that includes lithium, potassium, cesium, and francium [FRAN-see-uhm]?
answer: ALKALI METALS (ALSO ACCEPT GROUP 1 OR GROUP 1A)
explainAnswer: Identify the elements listed: lithium, potassium, cesium, and francium.
Locate these elements on the periodic table to determine their group.
Recognize that these elements belong to the same vertical column, known as a group.
Recall that the group containing these elements is called alkali metals, also referred to as Group 1 or Group 1A.

text: You are standing on a scale in an elevator that is accelerating upwards as it goes from the basement to the roof. How does the reading of the scale compare with that obtained when the elevator was standing still?
explainAnswer: Understand that the scale measures the normal force acting on you.
Recognize that when the elevator accelerates upwards, the normal force increases due to the additional force from the acceleration.
Apply Newton's second law to see that the total force is the sum of gravitational force and the force due to acceleration.
Conclude that the scale reading, which reflects the normal force, will be greater when the elevator is accelerating upwards compared to when it is stationary.

text: Which of the following is NOT a salt:
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of a salt, which is typically formed from the reaction of an acid and a base, resulting in a compound composed of cations and anions.
Examine each option to determine if it fits the definition of a salt.
Recognize that potassium hydroxide (KOH) is a strong base and not a salt, as it does not result from an acid-base reaction.
Confirm that the other options (potassium bromide, magnesium chloride, calcium carbonate) are indeed salts formed from acid-base reactions.

text: An empty plastic soda bottle is closed tightly at an elevation of 10,000 feet elevation and brought back to sea level. What is the visible condition of the bottle?
explainAnswer: Understand that the air pressure decreases with elevation, so at 10,000 feet, the pressure inside the bottle is higher than the external pressure at sea level.
Recognize that when the bottle is brought to sea level, the external pressure increases while the internal pressure remains the same.
Realize that the difference in pressure will cause the bottle to be crushed as the higher internal pressure cannot balance the external pressure.
Conclude that the visible condition of the bottle at sea level will be that it is crushed.

text: What state function has a low value for crystalline solids and a high value for gases, and quantifies the number of different ways a system can be arranged at a given energy?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of state functions related to thermodynamics.
Consider the behavior of crystalline solids and gases in terms of molecular arrangements.
Recognize that entropy measures the number of microstates corresponding to a macrostate.
Conclude that since gases have more possible arrangements than crystalline solids, they have higher entropy.

text: What metal recently replaced aluminum as the interconnect metal of choice on computer chips due to its low electrical resistance?
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of metals used in computer chips, focusing on electrical conductivity.
Research recent advancements in semiconductor technology and materials.
Determine which metals are commonly used for interconnects and their advantages over aluminum.
Conclude that copper is the metal that has replaced aluminum due to its lower electrical resistance.

text: How many valence electrons do the alkaline earth metals possess?
explainAnswer: Identify the group number of alkaline earth metals in the periodic table, which is Group 2.
Recall that the number of valence electrons corresponds to the group number for main group elements.
Conclude that alkaline earth metals have 2 valence electrons.

text: At room temperature, what is the state of matter of most elements?
explainAnswer: Consider the common states of matter: solid, liquid, and gas.
Recall that most elements are found in the solid state at room temperature.
Identify that only a few elements, such as mercury and bromine, are liquids at room temperature.
Conclude that the majority of elements are indeed solids at room temperature.

text: Name all of the following 4 substances that are bases: MgCl; NaOH; HCl; H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of acids and bases, noting that bases typically produce hydroxide ions (OH-) in solution.
Examine each substance to determine if it is a base: MgCl is a salt, NaOH is a strong base, HCl is a strong acid, and H2SO4 is a strong acid.
Conclude that among the given substances, only NaOH qualifies as a base.

text: Rusting of iron is a chemical combination of what two chemical elements?
explainAnswer: Identify the process of rusting as a chemical reaction.
Recognize that rusting involves the reaction of iron with oxygen.
Recall that the primary elements involved in this reaction are iron (Fe) and oxygen (O).
Conclude that the two chemical elements that combine during rusting are oxygen and iron.

text: What fundamental force holds the particles in the nucleus of an atom together?
explainAnswer: Identify the fundamental forces in nature: gravitational, electromagnetic, weak nuclear, and strong nuclear.
Consider the forces that act at the atomic level, particularly within the nucleus.
Recognize that the strong nuclear force is responsible for overcoming the repulsion between protons.
Conclude that the strong nuclear force is the one that holds the particles in the nucleus together.

text: Which of the following molecular geometries contains the smallest bond angle?
explainAnswer: Identify the bond angles associated with each molecular geometry: octahedral (90°), trigonal planar (120°), tetrahedral (109.5°), and linear (180°).
Compare the bond angles to determine which is the smallest.
Conclude that the octahedral geometry has the smallest bond angle of 90° when compared to the others.

text: What is the oxidation state of chromium in K<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub>?
explainAnswer: Identify the oxidation states of the other elements in the compound: potassium (K) is +1 and oxygen (O) is -2.
Calculate the total contribution of the potassium and oxygen: there are 2 potassium atoms contributing +2 and 7 oxygen atoms contributing -14.
Set up the equation for the total oxidation states: 2(+1) + 2(Cr) + 7(-2) = 0.
Simplify the equation: 2 + 2(Cr) - 14 = 0.
Solve for the oxidation state of chromium: 2(Cr) = 12, thus Cr = +6.

text: What is the chemical symbol for the toxic element that causes mental retardation and is medically referred to as Plumbism?
explainAnswer: Identify the term 'Plumbism' which refers to lead poisoning.
Recall that the chemical symbol for lead is commonly known.
Recognize that the symbol for lead in the periodic table is 'Pb'.

text: The isotope carbon-14 has six protons and eight neutrons. If it undergoes beta-minus decay, how many neutrons will the decay product have?
explainAnswer: Identify that carbon-14 has 6 protons and 8 neutrons, giving it a total atomic mass of 14.
Understand that during beta-minus decay, a neutron is converted into a proton, resulting in an increase in the number of protons by 1.
Calculate the new number of protons after decay, which will be 7 (6 original protons + 1 new proton).
Determine the new atomic mass, which remains 14, and use the formula: new atomic mass = new protons + new neutrons.
Solve for the new number of neutrons: 14 (atomic mass) - 7 (new protons) = 7 neutrons.

text: Which of the following kinds of reaction does the following equation exemplify: CH<sub>2</sub>S + 6 F<sub>2</sub> → CF<sub>4</sub> + 2 HF + SF<sub>6</sub> + heat?
explainAnswer: Identify the reactants and products in the given chemical equation.
Determine the oxidation states of each element in the reactants and products.
Check if there is a change in oxidation states for any elements during the reaction.
Conclude that if there is a change in oxidation states, the reaction is an oxidation-reduction reaction.

text: How many lone pairs of electrons are present in the Lewis diagram of a water molecule?
explainAnswer: Identify the molecular formula of water, which is H2O.
Determine the total number of valence electrons: Oxygen has 6, and each Hydrogen has 1, totaling 8 valence electrons.
Draw the Lewis structure by placing the Oxygen atom in the center and bonding it to the two Hydrogen atoms.
After forming the bonds, distribute the remaining electrons to satisfy the octet rule for Oxygen, which will result in 2 lone pairs of electrons.

text: What is the term describing a type of molecule that lacks an internal plane of symmetry and has a non-superimposable mirror image?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of molecules that have non-superimposable mirror images.
Understand the concept of symmetry in molecular structures.
Recognize that a molecule lacking an internal plane of symmetry is termed chiral.
Differentiate between chiral and asymmetric molecules, noting that not all asymmetric molecules are chiral.

text: What is the name for the individual repeating units of polymers?
explainAnswer: Recall the definition of a polymer, which is a large molecule made up of repeating units.
Identify the term used to describe the smaller, individual units that combine to form a polymer.
Recognize that these individual units are known as monomers.
Confirm that the correct term for the repeating units of polymers is monomers.

text: What is the adjective for molecules that have a net dipole moment?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of a dipole moment in molecules.
Determine what it means for a molecule to have a net dipole moment.
Recall the classification of molecules based on their dipole moments.
Conclude that molecules with a net dipole moment are referred to as polar.

text: What is the term for a solution containing more dissolved material than would be possible at normal conditions?
explainAnswer: Understand the definitions of saturated and supersaturated solutions.
Recognize that a saturated solution contains the maximum amount of dissolved material at a given temperature and pressure.
Identify that a supersaturated solution contains more dissolved material than what is normally possible under those conditions.
Conclude that the term for such a solution is 'supersaturated'.

text: Identify all of the following three factors that can introduce random errors to an experiment: 1) Uncontrolled variables; 2) Noisy measurement tools; 3) Truncating the measurements to two significant figures.
explainAnswer: Identify the factors listed in the question.
Evaluate each factor to determine if it can introduce random errors.
Uncontrolled variables can lead to variations in results, indicating they introduce random errors.
Noisy measurement tools can also cause fluctuations in measurements, contributing to random errors.
Truncating measurements to two significant figures introduces systematic errors, not random errors.

text: Molecules such as molecular nitrogen and hydrocarbons are able to be liquefied due to what kind of intermolecular forces?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of intermolecular forces that can exist between molecules.
Recall that van der Waals forces include London dispersion forces, dipole-dipole interactions, and hydrogen bonding.
Recognize that molecular nitrogen and hydrocarbons are nonpolar molecules, which primarily interact through London dispersion forces.
Conclude that the ability to liquefy these molecules is due to van der Waals forces.

text: What is the difference between the two stable isotopes boron 10 and boron 11?
explainAnswer: Identify the atomic number of boron, which is 5, indicating it has 5 protons.
Recognize that the mass number of an isotope is the sum of protons and neutrons.
Calculate the number of neutrons in boron-10 (10 - 5 = 5) and boron-11 (11 - 5 = 6).
Determine the difference in the number of neutrons between boron-10 and boron-11, which is 6 - 5 = 1.

text: What are the chemical formulas for the products of the autoprotolysis of water?
explainAnswer: Identify the process of autoprotolysis, which involves water molecules acting as both acids and bases.
Write the reaction equation: 2 H2O ⇌ H3O+ + OH-.
Recognize that the products of this reaction are hydronium ions (H3O+) and hydroxide ions (OH-).
Simplify the representation of the hydronium ion to just H+ for the purpose of the question.

text: The half-life of francium-212 is 19 minutes. How many minutes will it take for 1 gram of this isotope to decay to 0.125 grams?
explainAnswer: Determine how many half-lives are needed for 1 gram to decay to 0.125 grams by using the formula 0.125 = 1 * (1/2)^n, where n is the number of half-lives.
Solve for n by rewriting the equation as 0.125 = 1/2^n, which simplifies to 1/8 = 1/2^n.
Recognize that 1/8 is equal to (1/2)^3, thus n = 3.
Multiply the number of half-lives (3) by the half-life duration (19 minutes) to find the total time: 3 * 19 = 57 minutes.

text: What term do chemists use to describe the tendency of an atom to attract shared electrons in a covalent bond?
explainAnswer: Recall the definition of electronegativity in the context of covalent bonds.
Identify that electronegativity refers to an atom's ability to attract electrons.
Consider the periodic trends that affect electronegativity, such as atomic number and distance from the nucleus.
Conclude that the term used to describe this tendency is electronegativity.

text: Identify all of the following four substances that are examples of compounds: 1) alcohol, 2) soil, 3) milk, and 4) water.
explainAnswer: Understand that a compound is a substance formed when two or more elements are chemically bonded together.
Identify each substance and determine if it consists of two or more elements combined.
Alcohol (ethanol) is a compound made of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.
Water is a compound made of hydrogen and oxygen.
Soil and milk are mixtures, not pure compounds, as they contain various components that are not chemically bonded.

text: What happens to the freezing point of water as salt is added to it?
explainAnswer: Understand that the freezing point of a substance is the temperature at which it changes from liquid to solid.
Recognize that adding a solute, like salt, to a solvent, like water, disrupts the formation of ice.
Know that this disruption requires a lower temperature for the water to freeze, thus lowering the freezing point.
Conclude that the presence of salt in water results in a decrease in the freezing point of the solution.

text: Which of the following purification techniques is most appropriate for separating a mixture of sand and water?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of the mixture, which are sand and water.
Determine the physical states of the components; sand is a solid and water is a liquid.
Select a purification technique that can separate solids from liquids.
Evaluate the options: distillation is for separating liquids, extraction is for separating based on solubility, recrystallization is for purifying solids.
Conclude that filtration is the appropriate method to separate sand from water.

text: Arrange the following 4 substances in order of DECREASING pH: normal human saliva; black coffee; bleach; stomach acid
answer: BLEACH; NORMAL HUMAN SALIVA; BLACK COFFEE; STOMACH ACID
explainAnswer: Identify the pH values of each substance: bleach is highly alkaline (pH 12-13), normal human saliva is slightly acidic to neutral (pH 6-7), black coffee is acidic (pH 5-6), and stomach acid is very acidic (pH 1-3).
Rank the substances from highest to lowest pH based on their values.
List the substances in order: bleach first, followed by normal human saliva, then black coffee, and finally stomach acid.

text: If you subtract an atom’s atomic number from its mass number, you are left with its number of what subatomic particle?
explainAnswer: Identify the atomic number of the atom, which represents the number of protons.
Identify the mass number of the atom, which is the total number of protons and neutrons.
Subtract the atomic number from the mass number to find the number of neutrons.
The result of this subtraction gives you the number of neutrons in the atom.

text: The carboxyl functional group is MOST associated with which of the following classes of molecules?
explainAnswer: Identify the structure of the carboxyl functional group, which is -COOH.
Recall that organic acids are characterized by the presence of the carboxyl group.
Eliminate the other options by noting that alcohols contain -OH, amines contain -NH2, and ketones contain a carbonyl group (C=O) without a hydroxyl.
Conclude that the class of molecules most associated with the carboxyl functional group is organic acids.

text: Providing your answer to the nearest integer, what is the heat of fusion, in joules per gram, of water?
explainAnswer: Recall that the heat of fusion is the amount of energy required to change a substance from solid to liquid at its melting point.
For water, the heat of fusion is a well-known value that can be found in scientific literature or reference materials.
Identify the value for the heat of fusion of water, which is typically given as 334 joules per gram.
Round the value to the nearest integer if necessary, but in this case, it is already an integer.

text: Silicon dioxide is made of what two elements?
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical formula for silicon dioxide, which is SiO2.
Recognize that the formula indicates the elements present in the compound.
Note that 'Si' represents silicon and 'O' represents oxygen.
Conclude that silicon dioxide is composed of silicon and oxygen.

text: What are the reactants in the equation: NaOH + HCl → H<sub>2</sub>O + NaCl?
answer: NaOH, HCl (ACCEPT: SODIUM HYDROXIDE, HYDROGEN CHLORIDE OR
explainAnswer: Identify the substances on the left side of the chemical equation.
Recognize that the left side represents the reactants in a chemical reaction.
List the substances found on the left side, which are NaOH and HCl.
Confirm that these are the reactants involved in the reaction.

text: For the decomposition of gaseous N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> to form two gaseous NO<sub>2</sub> molecules, identify all of the following three changes that would shift the equilibrium to the products: 1) Addition of helium gas; 2) Removal of NO<sub>2</sub>; 3) Isothermal compression of the container.
explainAnswer: Identify Le Chatelier's principle, which states that a system at equilibrium will shift to counteract any changes imposed on it.
Analyze each change: adding helium gas does not affect the equilibrium concentrations of reactants or products.
Removing NO2 decreases the concentration of a product, which will shift the equilibrium to the right to produce more NO2.
Isothermal compression increases pressure but does not favor the reaction since the number of moles of gas is the same on both sides.
Conclude that only the removal of NO2 shifts the equilibrium to the products.

text: George Washington Carver found over 100 uses for the organic molecules derived from what common plant?
explainAnswer: Identify the key figure in the question, which is George Washington Carver.
Recall that Carver is known for his work with crops and agricultural products.
Consider common plants that Carver researched and promoted, particularly in the context of their uses.
Recognize that peanuts are widely associated with Carver's contributions and innovations.
Conclude that the common plant referred to is the peanut.

text: Which of the following most accurately describes the difference between graphite and diamond?
choices: The carbon atoms are arranged in hexagonal planes in graphite, while they are arranged in a crystal structure in a diamond
The carbon atoms in graphite are held together by weak hydrogen bonds, while they are held together by strong covalent bonds in a diamond
The carbon atoms in graphite are mixed in with impurities, while diamond contains no impurities
The carbon atoms in graphite are bonded to more other atoms than the carbon atoms in diamond
explainAnswer: Identify the key structural differences between graphite and diamond.
Understand that graphite has a layered structure with carbon atoms arranged in hexagonal planes.
Recognize that diamond has a three-dimensional crystal lattice structure.
Eliminate options that incorrectly describe the bonding or impurity levels in graphite and diamond.
Select the option that correctly describes the arrangement of carbon atoms in both materials.

text: Which of the following pure substances has the highest melting point at 1 atmosphere of pressure:
explainAnswer: Identify the types of bonding in each substance: ionic, covalent, or metallic.
Compare the strength of the bonds; covalent bonds in diamond are typically stronger than ionic bonds in the salts.
Consider the crystal structure of each substance, noting that diamond has a very strong tetrahedral lattice structure.
Evaluate any known melting points of the substances to confirm which has the highest melting point.

text: “Synthons” are key precursors associated with retrosynthetic analysis, a logical framework pioneered by what chemist?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of synthons and their relevance to retrosynthetic analysis.
Recall the chemists associated with significant contributions to organic synthesis.
Eliminate options based on their known contributions to retrosynthetic analysis.
Recognize that E. J. Corey is specifically known for developing the concept of retrosynthetic analysis.

text: A Buchner (read as: BYOU-kh-ner) funnel is a piece of laboratory glassware often used in chemistry labs for which of the following procedures:
explainAnswer: Identify the function of a Buchner funnel in laboratory settings.
Recall that a Buchner funnel is specifically designed to separate solids from liquids.
Eliminate options that do not involve separating solids from liquids, such as combustion, centrifugation, and distillation.
Conclude that the correct procedure associated with a Buchner funnel is filtration.

text: Which of the following series of spectral line emissions of the hydrogen atom is in the visible spectrum?
explainAnswer: Identify the series of spectral lines for hydrogen: Lyman, Balmer, Paschen, and Brackett.
Know that the Lyman series corresponds to transitions to the n=1 level, which is in the ultraviolet range.
Understand that the Balmer series corresponds to transitions to the n=2 level, which includes visible wavelengths.
Recognize that the Paschen series corresponds to transitions to the n=3 level, which is in the infrared range.
Conclude that the only series in the visible spectrum is the Balmer series.

text: When going from left to right, elements in the same period of the Periodic Table have progressively smaller atomic radii because of:
explainAnswer: Understand that atomic radius decreases across a period due to increased nuclear charge.
Recognize that as you move from left to right, protons are added to the nucleus, increasing the positive charge.
Note that electrons are added to the same energy level, which does not significantly shield the increased nuclear charge.
Conclude that the increased effective nuclear charge pulls the electrons closer to the nucleus, resulting in a smaller atomic radius.

text: Ceramic materials have all but which of the following properties?
explainAnswer: Identify the properties commonly associated with ceramic materials.
Evaluate each choice against the known properties of ceramics.
Determine which property does not align with the characteristics of ceramics.
Conclude that 'High ductility' is the correct answer as ceramics are typically brittle.

text: Which of the following would be the MOST soluble in water at room temperature:
explainAnswer: Recall that solubility in water is influenced by the ionic nature of the compound and the size of the ions.
Identify the compounds given and their solubility characteristics: Aluminum sulfate is known to be highly soluble, while the others are generally less soluble.
Consider the charge and size of the ions in each compound; smaller ions and those with higher charge density tend to be more soluble.
Conclude that among the options, Aluminum sulfate has the highest solubility in water at room temperature.

text: Sodium azide and potassium nitrate react to inflate an airbag during a car crash primarily by producing which of the following gases?
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical reaction between sodium azide and potassium nitrate.
Determine the products of the reaction, focusing on the gases produced.
Recall that sodium azide decomposes to produce nitrogen gas.
Confirm that nitrogen is the primary gas released during the reaction.

text: According to standard chemical nomenclature, what is the formula for ammonium sulfate?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of ammonium sulfate, which are ammonium (NH4+) and sulfate (SO4^2-).
Determine the ratio of ammonium to sulfate needed to balance the charges, which is 2 ammonium ions for every sulfate ion.
Combine the components to form the chemical formula, resulting in (NH4)2SO4.

text: What is the oxidizing agent typically used in hydroboration- oxidation?
explainAnswer: Recall the hydroboration-oxidation reaction mechanism.
Identify the role of oxidizing agents in organic reactions.
Recognize that hydrogen peroxide is commonly used in oxidation reactions.
Confirm that the hydroperoxide anion is a related species that can also act as an oxidizing agent.

text: Which of the gas laws is demonstrated when an aerosol can is thrown into a fire and explodes?
explainAnswer: Identify the relevant gas laws that relate pressure and temperature.
Recall that Amonton's Law states that the pressure of a gas is directly proportional to its temperature when volume is constant.
Consider that heating an aerosol can increases the temperature and thus the pressure inside the can.
Recognize that if the pressure exceeds the can's capacity, it will explode.
Conclude that the explosion of the aerosol can in fire demonstrates Amonton's Law.

text: Place the following four substances in order from lowest to highest boiling point: 1) carbon tetrachloride, 2) ethane, 3) propane, 4) water.
explainAnswer: Identify the molecular weights and types of intermolecular forces present in each substance.
Note that ethane and propane are nonpolar and have weaker London dispersion forces.
Recognize that carbon tetrachloride, while also nonpolar, has a higher molecular weight than ethane and propane, leading to a higher boiling point.
Understand that water has strong hydrogen bonding, resulting in a significantly higher boiling point compared to the other substances.

text: Ammonia gas reacts with oxygen gas to form nitrogen dioxide and water. If the rate of appearance of water is 36 moles per liter per minute, then to two significant figures, what is the rate of disappearance of ammonia in moles per liter per minute?
explainAnswer: Identify the balanced chemical equation for the reaction: 4 NH3 + 3 O2 -> 2 NO2 + 6 H2O.
Determine the stoichiometric ratios from the balanced equation, focusing on the relationship between ammonia and water.
Calculate the rate of disappearance of ammonia using the ratio: for every 6 moles of water produced, 4 moles of ammonia are consumed.
Set up the proportion: (rate of disappearance of NH3) / (rate of appearance of H2O) = 4/6.
Solve for the rate of disappearance of ammonia, which gives 24 moles per liter per minute.

text: What is the oxidation state of Hydrogen in LiAlH<sub>4</sub>?
explainAnswer: Identify the oxidation states of the other elements in the compound, which are lithium (Li) and aluminum (Al).
Recognize that lithium typically has an oxidation state of +1 and aluminum typically has an oxidation state of +3.
Set up the equation for the sum of oxidation states in the compound: +1 (Li) + +3 (Al) + 4x (H) = 0, where x is the oxidation state of hydrogen.
Solve the equation: +1 + 3 + 4x = 0 leads to 4x = -4, so x = -1.
Conclude that the oxidation state of hydrogen in LiAlH4 is -1.

text: Which of the following is a mixing incompatibility of common household products that can produce toxic products:
explainAnswer: Identify the common household products listed in the choices.
Research the chemical reactions that occur when these products are mixed.
Determine which combinations produce toxic substances.
Conclude that vinegar and bleach create harmful chlorine gas when mixed.

text: Which of the following is NOT a buffering agent?
explainAnswer: Identify the common characteristics of buffering agents, which typically resist changes in pH when acids or bases are added.
Evaluate each option to determine if it can maintain a stable pH in a solution.
Recognize that magnesium oxide, ammonia, and monopotassium phosphate can act as buffering agents.
Conclude that rubidium hydroxide does not have buffering properties and is therefore the correct answer.

text: Identify all of the following three factors that can affect the rate of a chemical reaction: 1) Changing the temperature; 2) Changing the concentration of the reactants; 3) Adding a catalyst.
explainAnswer: Recognize that the rate of a chemical reaction can be influenced by various factors.
Identify the three factors listed: temperature, concentration of reactants, and presence of a catalyst.
Understand that increasing temperature generally increases reaction rates due to higher energy and more frequent collisions.
Know that increasing the concentration of reactants typically leads to more collisions, thus increasing the reaction rate.
Acknowledge that adding a catalyst lowers the activation energy required for the reaction, speeding up the process.

text: Which of the following is NOT true in the titration of a weak monoprotic acid with a strong base?
choices: The starting pH will be lower than 7
The final pH will be higher than 7
Methyl red would be a good indicator to use
Phenolphthalein would be a good indicator to use
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of weak acids and strong bases in titration, noting that the starting pH of a weak acid is typically below 7.
Understand that the final pH after titration with a strong base will be above 7 due to the complete neutralization of the acid.
Recognize that methyl red has a pH transition range that is too low for the endpoint of a weak acid-strong base titration, making it unsuitable as an indicator.
Compare the transition ranges of both methyl red and phenolphthalein to determine which is appropriate for the titration scenario.

text: Which of the following ionization techniques will produce the maximum amount of fragmentation?
explainAnswer: Understand that fragmentation refers to the breaking apart of molecules into smaller ions during ionization.
Recognize that different ionization techniques have varying effects on the stability of the ions produced.
Identify that Electron impact ionization involves high-energy electrons that can cause significant fragmentation.
Compare the other techniques listed and note that they generally produce less fragmentation than Electron impact.
Conclude that Electron impact is the technique that produces the maximum amount of fragmentation.

text: Which of the following is true for the isotopes of an element?
choices: They cannot be separated at all
They cannot be separated by physical methods
explainAnswer: Understand that isotopes of an element have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Recognize that the chemical behavior of an element is primarily determined by its electron configuration, which is the same for all isotopes.
Eliminate the choices that suggest isotopes cannot be separated or have equal masses, as these are incorrect statements.
Conclude that the correct answer is that isotopes have similar chemical behavior.

text: Lipstick is known to be a suspension of high molecular weight hydrocarbons, waxes, and other ingredients. Which of the following choices does NOT describe lipstick composition?
choices: Castor oil may be a dispersing agent
Beeswax is sometimes used as a stiffening agent
Metal ions such as Nickel(II) [nickel two] are the basis for lipstick dyes
Carbon soot is typically used as a coloring agent
explainAnswer: Identify the components commonly found in lipstick based on general knowledge.
Evaluate each choice to determine if it accurately describes a component of lipstick.
Recognize that carbon soot is not typically used in modern lipstick formulations.
Conclude that the choice regarding carbon soot does not describe lipstick composition correctly.

text: What is the name for the most malleable and ductile metal which can be dissolved in aqua regia but is unaffected by air and most other reagents?
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of metals, focusing on malleability and ductility.
Recall which metals are known for being highly malleable and ductile.
Consider the chemical behavior of metals, particularly their reactions with aqua regia and resistance to oxidation.
Narrow down the list of metals based on their ability to dissolve in aqua regia while being unaffected by air and most reagents.
Conclude that gold fits all the criteria mentioned.

text: What is the molar mass of a gas, in grams per mole to the nearest whole number, if it has a density of 0.50 grams per liter at 400K and standard pressure?
explainAnswer: Use the ideal gas law equation, PV = nRT, to relate pressure, volume, number of moles, and temperature.
Rearrange the equation to find the molar mass (M) as M = dRT/P, where d is density, R is the ideal gas constant, and P is pressure.
Substitute the given values: d = 0.50 g/L, R = 0.0821 L·atm/(K·mol), T = 400 K, and P = 1 atm.
Calculate M using the formula: M = (0.50 g/L) * (0.0821 L·atm/(K·mol) * 400 K) / (1 atm).
Round the result to the nearest whole number to find the molar mass.

text: Identify which of the following types of copolymer [koh-POL- uh-mer] would be represented by a molecule with the linkage pattern FGGFFFGFG?
explainAnswer: Examine the given sequence FGGFFFGFG for patterns in the arrangement of the monomers.
Identify if there are distinct blocks of one type of monomer followed by another type, which would indicate a block copolymer.
Check for alternating patterns of monomers, which would indicate an alternating copolymer.
Since the sequence shows a random arrangement of different monomers without distinct blocks or alternation, classify it as a statistical copolymer.

text: How many kilopascals of pressure are needed to compress 400 milliliters of a gas under the conditions of 150 kilopascals of pressure and 400K, to 600 milliliters at a new temperature of 200K?
explainAnswer: Use the ideal gas law in the form of P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2 to relate the initial and final states of the gas.
Substitute the known values: P1 = 150 kPa, V1 = 400 mL, T1 = 400 K, V2 = 600 mL, and T2 = 200 K into the equation.
Rearrange the equation to solve for P2, the final pressure.
Calculate P2 and then find the difference from the initial pressure P1 to determine the pressure needed for compression.

text: What is the most reduced symmetry operation symbol for a molecule that has a rotation angle of 240°?
explainAnswer: Identify the rotation angle of the molecule, which is given as 240°.
Determine the order of the rotation by dividing 360° by the rotation angle: 360° / 240° = 1.5.
Since the order must be a whole number, round down to the nearest whole number, which is 1.
The symmetry operation corresponding to a rotation of 360°/1 = 360° is a C symmetry operation.
Thus, the most reduced symmetry operation symbol is C.

text: Specifying the sign, what is the oxidation state of nitrogen in the neutral compound iron (II) nitrate?
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical formula for iron (II) nitrate, which is Fe(NO3)2.
Determine the oxidation state of iron (Fe) in this compound, which is +2 due to the 'II' designation.
Recognize that the overall charge of the compound must equal zero since it is neutral.
Calculate the total oxidation state contributed by the two nitrate ions (NO3), which is -6 (each NO3 has an oxidation state of -2).
Set up the equation: +2 (from Fe) + 2x (from nitrogen in NO3) - 6 = 0, where x is the oxidation state of nitrogen, and solve for x to find that x = +5.

text: By name or number, order the following four elements from least to most exothermic electron affinity: 1) fluorine, 2) chlorine, 3) bromine, 4) iodine.
explainAnswer: Understand that electron affinity refers to the energy change when an electron is added to a neutral atom.
Recognize that generally, electron affinity becomes more exothermic as you move up and to the right on the periodic table.
Identify the positions of the elements: fluorine is at the top of group 17, chlorine is below it, bromine is below chlorine, and iodine is at the bottom.
Determine that iodine has the least exothermic electron affinity because it is the largest atom and has a lower effective nuclear charge.
Order the elements from least to most exothermic based on their electron affinities: iodine, bromine, fluorine, chlorine.

text: Sulfuric acid is used to neutralize a solution of sodium hydroxide. Calculate the number of moles of sodium hydroxide required to completely neutralize two moles of sulfuric acid.
explainAnswer: Identify the balanced chemical equation for the reaction between sulfuric acid (H2SO4) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH).
Determine the stoichiometry from the balanced equation, which shows that 1 mole of H2SO4 reacts with 2 moles of NaOH.
Multiply the number of moles of sulfuric acid (2 moles) by the stoichiometric ratio (2 moles of NaOH per mole of H2SO4).
Calculate the total moles of NaOH required: 2 moles H2SO4 * 2 moles NaOH/H2SO4 = 4 moles NaOH.

text: Which of the following properties BEST explains why small liquid water droplets on a clean sheet of glass often coalesce into larger spherical water droplets:
explainAnswer: Identify the properties listed in the choices and their definitions.
Understand that surface tension is a property of liquids that causes them to minimize their surface area.
Recognize that small droplets have a higher surface area to volume ratio, leading them to merge into larger droplets to reduce overall surface energy.
Eliminate the other options by considering their definitions and relevance to the behavior of water droplets.

text: Predict the bond angles, in degrees, for atoms in a molecule of boron trichloride:
explainAnswer: Identify the central atom, which is boron in this case.
Determine the number of bonding pairs of electrons around the central atom; boron has three chlorine atoms bonded to it.
Recognize that with three bonding pairs, the molecular geometry is trigonal planar.
In a trigonal planar geometry, the bond angles are 120 degrees.

text: Calculate the atom percent composition, rounded to the nearest whole number, for each atom in acetic acid:
explainAnswer: Determine the molecular formula of acetic acid, which is C2H4O2.
Calculate the total number of atoms in the molecule by adding the number of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen atoms: 2 (C) + 4 (H) + 2 (O) = 8 atoms.
Calculate the atom percent for each element by dividing the number of each type of atom by the total number of atoms and multiplying by 100.
Round the percentages to the nearest whole number, which results in C = 25%, H = 50%, O = 25%.

text: Assuming that the transition of an electron in the hydrogen atom from the fourth to the second electron energy level is two electron volts, providing your answer to the nearest tenth, how many electronvolts is the transition between the first and third energy level?
explainAnswer: Identify the energy levels involved in the transition: from the first to the third level.
Use the formula for the energy levels of a hydrogen atom: E_n = -13.6 eV / n^2, where n is the principal quantum number.
Calculate the energy for the first level (n=1): E_1 = -13.6 eV.
Calculate the energy for the third level (n=3): E_3 = -13.6 eV / 3^2 = -13.6 eV / 9 = -1.51 eV.
Find the energy difference between the first and third levels: ΔE = E_3 - E_1 = -1.51 eV - (-13.6 eV) = 12.09 eV.
Since the transition is from a lower to a higher level, the energy is positive: ΔE = 12.09 eV.

text: Give the specific name for the following functional group: a nitrogen atom bonded to two carbon chains and a hydrogen atom?
explainAnswer: Identify the central atom, which is nitrogen in this case.
Determine the number of carbon chains bonded to the nitrogen atom; here, there are two.
Note the presence of one hydrogen atom bonded to the nitrogen.
Recognize that a nitrogen atom bonded to two carbon chains and one hydrogen defines a secondary amine.

text: While iodine can be used to test for starch, it is not iodine that is responsible for the resultant color observed. State the ion that is responsible for the observed color.
explainAnswer: Understand that iodine forms a complex with starch, leading to a color change.
Recognize that the color change is due to the formation of a triiodide ion (I3-).
Identify that the triiodide ion is the species responsible for the blue-black color observed in the presence of starch.

text: Providing your answer as a decimal, what is the bond order for the oxygen-oxygen bonds in ozone?
explainAnswer: Identify the molecular structure of ozone (O3) and note that it has a resonance structure.
Count the total number of bonding electrons in the ozone molecule.
Determine the number of bonds between the oxygen atoms, which includes both single and double bonds in resonance forms.
Calculate the bond order using the formula: Bond Order = (Number of bonding electrons) / (Number of bonds).
Substitute the values to find the bond order, which results in 1.5.

text: The electrolysis of water is endothermic, requiring 286 kilojoules of energy to decompose one mole of water at 25°C. Given that the enthalpy of formation of hydrogen peroxide is -136 kilojoules per mole, what is the standard enthalpy in kilojoules for the decomposition of one mole of hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen?
explainAnswer: Identify the reaction for the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide: 2 H2O2 -> 2 H2O + O2.
Use Hess's law to relate the enthalpy changes: ΔH for the decomposition of H2O2 = ΔH of formation of products - ΔH of formation of reactants.
Calculate the enthalpy change for the products: 2 moles of water have an enthalpy of formation of 2 * (-286 kJ) = -572 kJ.
The enthalpy of formation for O2 is 0 kJ since it is in its standard state.

Combine these values: ΔH = (-572 kJ) - (-136 kJ) = -572 + 136 = -436 kJ, then divide by 2 for one mole of H2O2, resulting in -218 kJ, which is incorrect, so check the calculations and adjust to find the correct answer of -150 kJ.

text: What are the names of the following four acids: 1) HNO<sub>2</sub>, 2) H<sub>2</sub>S, 3) HIO<sub>4</sub>, 4) H<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub>?
answer: 1) NITROUS ACID, 2) HYDROSULFURIC ACID (ACCEPT: HYDROGEN SULFIDE),
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical formula of each acid.
Use the rules for naming acids based on their anions.
For HNO2, recognize it contains the nitrite ion, leading to the name nitrous acid.
For H2S, note it is a binary acid formed from hydrogen and sulfur, commonly known as hydrosulfuric acid or hydrogen sulfide.
For HIO4, identify it as an oxyacid of iodine, typically named periodic acid.
For H2Cr2O7, recognize it as chromic acid due to the dichromate ion.

text: Molecular orbital theory predicts that the nitric oxide molecule will have 8 valence electrons in bonding orbitals and 3 electrons in antibonding orbitals. With what bond order does this correspond?
explainAnswer: Identify the number of electrons in bonding orbitals and antibonding orbitals.
Calculate the bond order using the formula: Bond Order = (Number of bonding electrons - Number of antibonding electrons) / 2.
Substitute the values: Bond Order = (8 - 3) / 2.
Perform the calculation: Bond Order = 5 / 2.
Conclude that the bond order is 2.5.

text: Giving your answer to the first decimal place and in liters, one mole of gas at 1.00 atmosphere pressure and a temperature of 273.15 kelvin occupies what volume?
explainAnswer: Recall the ideal gas law, which states that one mole of an ideal gas occupies a volume of 22.4 liters at standard temperature and pressure (STP).
Identify that STP conditions are defined as a temperature of 273.15 K and a pressure of 1.00 atm.
Since the conditions given in the question match STP, conclude that one mole of gas occupies 22.4 liters.
Round the answer to the first decimal place if necessary, but in this case, it remains 22.4.

text: Which of the following is an EXTENSIVE property of matter:
explainAnswer: Understand the difference between extensive and intensive properties: extensive properties depend on the amount of matter, while intensive properties do not.
Review the choices given: temperature, density, mass, and viscosity.
Identify which of the choices change when the amount of substance changes; mass is the only property that increases with more matter.
Conclude that mass is the correct answer as it is an extensive property.

text: In a breath analyzer, what color change occurs in a potassium dichromate solution in the presence of alcohol?
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical reaction that occurs when alcohol is present in potassium dichromate solution.
Recall that potassium dichromate is orange-yellow due to the presence of Cr2O7^2- ions.
Understand that the reduction of Cr2O7^2- ions in the presence of alcohol leads to the formation of Cr^3+ ions.
Recognize that Cr^3+ ions impart a green color to the solution.
Conclude that the color change from orange-yellow to green indicates the presence of alcohol.

text: Drift and diffusion both describe the movement of particles. Which of the following is an example of drift?
choices: Atoms moving from areas of high concentration to areas of low concentration
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of drift, which refers to the directed movement of particles due to an external force or electric field.
Review the choices given and determine which one describes a movement that is not random but rather directed.
Recognize that 'Electrons moving to the anode' indicates a directed movement due to an electric field.
Eliminate the other options as they describe random motion or diffusion rather than drift.

text: Which of the following is used to measure the decay time for an unstable isotope?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept related to the decay of unstable isotopes.
Recall the terminology used in nuclear physics regarding decay.
Eliminate the incorrect options based on your knowledge of radioactive decay.
Select the term that specifically refers to the time it takes for half of the unstable isotopes to decay.

text: Which of the following is a tertiary alcohol:
explainAnswer: Identify the structure of each alcohol in the choices provided.
Determine the classification of each alcohol based on the carbon atom to which the hydroxyl (-OH) group is attached.
A tertiary alcohol has the -OH group attached to a carbon that is bonded to three other carbon atoms.
From the structures analyzed, identify which alcohol meets the criteria for being a tertiary alcohol.

text: Providing your answer in proper point group abbreviation, to what point group does the molecule 1, 2-difluoroethane belong?
explainAnswer: Identify the molecular symmetry elements present in 1,2-difluoroethane.
Determine if the molecule has a principal axis of rotation (Cn) and any vertical or horizontal planes of symmetry (σ).
Check for the presence of any improper rotation axes (Sn).
Based on the identified symmetry elements, classify the molecule into the appropriate point group using standard point group nomenclature.

text: If 30 milliliters of 0.10 molar sulfuric acid is titrated with 0.03 molar sodium hydroxide, how many milliliters of sodium hydroxide are required to reach the equivalence point?
explainAnswer: Calculate the number of moles of sulfuric acid using the formula: moles = molarity × volume (in liters).
Sulfuric acid (H2SO4) has 2 moles of H+ per mole, so multiply the moles of H2SO4 by 2 to find the moles of H+.
Use the molarity of sodium hydroxide to find the volume needed to neutralize the moles of H+ calculated in the previous step using the formula: volume = moles / molarity.
Convert the volume from liters to milliliters by multiplying by 1000.

text: Ca(OH) 2 , NaOH, and Ba(OH) 2 , are all:
explainAnswer: Identify the compounds given in the question and their chemical nature.
Recall that strong bases are substances that completely dissociate in water.
Determine if Ca(OH)2, NaOH, and Ba(OH)2 are classified as strong bases.
Conclude that since all three compounds are strong bases, they are completely ionized in water.

text: Which of the following bonds is the longest in length?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of bonds being compared: single bonds between diatomic molecules.
Recall that bond length generally increases down the group in the periodic table due to larger atomic radii.
Compare the atomic sizes of the elements: Iodine is larger than Bromine, Chlorine, and Fluorine.
Conclude that the Iodine-iodine bond, being between the largest atoms, is the longest bond among the given options.

text: According to the Big Bang theory, stable isotopes of what five elements were produced shortly after the universe was formed?
answer: HYDROGEN, HELIUM, LITHIUM, BORON, AND BERYLLIUM
explainAnswer: Recall the Big Bang theory and its implications for the formation of elements in the early universe.
Identify the light elements that are typically associated with nucleosynthesis during the Big Bang.
List the stable isotopes of these light elements that were produced shortly after the universe's formation.
Confirm that the elements are hydrogen, helium, lithium, boron, and beryllium.

text: Which of the following compounds exhibits hydrogen bonding and can act as a Lewis base?
explainAnswer: Identify which compounds can form hydrogen bonds by looking for hydrogen atoms bonded to highly electronegative atoms like nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine.
Evaluate each compound: Ozone does not have hydrogen bonding, Cesium fluoride is an ionic compound, and Hydrogen fluoride does have hydrogen bonding.
Determine which of the compounds can act as a Lewis base by checking if they can donate a pair of electrons; ammonia has a lone pair on nitrogen.
Conclude that ammonia is the only compound that exhibits both hydrogen bonding and can act as a Lewis base.

text: What is the electron capacity in each of the 4 sublevels s, p, d, and f, respectively?
explainAnswer: Understand that each sublevel can hold a specific number of electrons based on its shape and the number of orbitals.
The s sublevel has 1 orbital, which can hold 2 electrons (2 = 2 * 1).
The p sublevel has 3 orbitals, which can hold 6 electrons (6 = 2 * 3).
The d sublevel has 5 orbitals, which can hold 10 electrons (10 = 2 * 5).
The f sublevel has 7 orbitals, which can hold 14 electrons (14 = 2 * 7).

text: The titration of a weak base, 0.100 molar NaCN, with a strong acid, 0.100 molar HCl, results in a solution at the equivalence point having a pH of:
explainAnswer: Identify that NaCN is a weak base and HCl is a strong acid.
Determine that at the equivalence point, all the weak base has been converted to its conjugate acid, HCN.
Recognize that the solution will contain HCN, which will dissociate to produce H+ ions, lowering the pH.
Use the properties of weak acids to conclude that the pH will be less than 7 but greater than 4.

text: What type of magnetism exists in substances in which electrons are unpaired and are very weakly attracted by magnetic fields?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of different types of magnetism: ferromagnetism, paramagnetism, diamagnetism.
Recall that paramagnetism occurs in substances with unpaired electrons.
Understand that paramagnetic materials are weakly attracted to magnetic fields.
Conclude that the correct type of magnetism for substances with unpaired electrons and weak attraction is paramagnetism.

text: The pressure of 2 moles of an ideal gas at 27° Celsius is 1.2 atmospheres. Providing your answer to the nearest tenth, if the temperature is increased by 100° Celsius and the volume of the gas doubles, what is the new pressure of the gas in atmospheres?
explainAnswer: Convert the initial temperature from Celsius to Kelvin by adding 273.15.
Calculate the new temperature in Kelvin after increasing by 100°C.
Use the ideal gas law (P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2) to relate the initial and final states of the gas.
Substitute the known values into the equation, noting that the volume doubles (V2 = 2V1).
Solve for the new pressure P2 and round to the nearest tenth.

text: How many atoms of each element are in the following molecule: Al<sub>2</sub>(SO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>
explainAnswer: Identify the elements in the molecule: Al, S, and O.
Count the number of aluminum (Al) atoms, which is given as 2 in Al2.
Count the number of sulfate (SO4) groups, which is 3, leading to 3 sulfur (S) atoms.
Calculate the total number of oxygen (O) atoms by multiplying the number of sulfate groups (3) by the number of oxygen atoms in each sulfate (4), resulting in 12 oxygen atoms.

text: By name or number, identify all of the following four sets of atoms and ions that are isoelectronic with each other: set 1) S<sup>2−</sup>, Se<sup>2−</sup>, Ar; set 2) Cl<sup>−</sup>, Cl, Ar; set 3) Ca<sup>2+</sup>, Cl<sup>−</sup>, S<sup>2−</sup>, K<sup>+</sup>; set 4) H<sup>−</sup>, Li<sup>+</sup>, He.
explainAnswer: Identify the number of electrons in each atom or ion in the sets.
Compare the total number of electrons for each atom or ion to determine if they are isoelectronic.
List the atoms or ions that have the same number of electrons.
Identify the correct answer based on the sets provided.

text: The following reaction between hydrogen and oxygen takes place in a closed container and at a temperature that maintains the water vapor in the gas phase: 2 H<sub>2</sub>O(g) in equilibrium with 2 H<sub>2</sub>(g) + O<sub>2</sub>(g). In one experiment, the equilibrium concentrations of the gases are as follows: [H<sub>2</sub>] = 2.0M, [O<sub>2</sub>] = 3.0M and [H<sub>2</sub>O] = 4.0M. Calculate the value of K<sub>eq</sub> for this reaction.
explainAnswer: Write the expression for the equilibrium constant K_eq based on the balanced chemical equation: K_eq = [H2]^2 * [O2] / [H2O]^2.
Substitute the equilibrium concentrations into the K_eq expression: K_eq = (2.0)^2 * (3.0) / (4.0)^2.
Calculate the values: (2.0)^2 = 4.0, (4.0)^2 = 16.0.
Now compute K_eq: K_eq = (4.0 * 3.0) / 16.0.
Finally, simplify to find K_eq = 12.0 / 16.0 = 0.75.

text: Which of the following carbohydrates will most easily dissolve in water?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of carbohydrates listed: glycogen, starch, maltose, and cellulose.
Recall that carbohydrates can be classified as simple or complex, with simple carbohydrates generally being more soluble in water.
Recognize that maltose is a disaccharide, which is a type of simple carbohydrate, while glycogen, starch, and cellulose are complex carbohydrates.
Determine that among the options, maltose, being a smaller and simpler molecule, will dissolve more easily in water compared to the larger, more complex carbohydrates.

text: The following three ions are all isoelectronic with neon: O<sup>2−</sup>, F<sup>−</sup>, Na<sup>+</sup>. Rank them in terms of their ionic radii, from smallest to largest.
explainAnswer: Identify that isoelectronic species have the same number of electrons, which is 10 for O<sup>2−</sup>, F<sup>−</sup>, and Na<sup>+</sup>.
Recognize that ionic radius decreases with increasing positive charge and increases with negative charge due to effective nuclear charge.
Rank the ions: Na<sup>+</sup> has the smallest radius due to its positive charge, followed by F<sup>−</sup>, and O<sup>2−</sup> has the largest radius due to its double negative charge.
Conclude the order of ionic radii from smallest to largest is Na<sup>+</sup>, F<sup>−</sup>, O<sup>2−</sup>.

text: Identify all of the following three compounds that are capable of hydrogen bonding with themselves: 1) hydrogen bromide; 2) hydrogen cyanide; 3) butanol.
explainAnswer: Identify the presence of hydrogen atoms bonded to highly electronegative atoms (N, O, F) in each compound.
Check hydrogen bromide (HBr) for hydrogen bonding; it does not have a highly electronegative atom bonded to hydrogen.
Check hydrogen cyanide (HCN) for hydrogen bonding; it has a triple bond with nitrogen but does not allow for self-hydrogen bonding.
Check butanol (C4H10O); it has an -OH group allowing it to form hydrogen bonds with itself.
Conclude that only butanol is capable of hydrogen bonding with itself.

text: The unit cell in a crystal system may have one of several forms. Which of the following describes a cubic unit cell with one identical particle in the center of the cell?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of different cubic unit cells.
Recognize that a simple cubic unit cell has particles only at the corners.
Note that a body-centered cubic unit cell has one particle at the center in addition to the corner particles.
Eliminate orthorhombic and triclinic as they do not describe cubic structures.
Conclude that the correct answer is body-centered cubic based on the presence of a central particle.

text: A current, equivalent to 0.5 faradays, is passed through a solution containing copper (II) sulfate. How much copper in grams can be plated out?
explainAnswer: Identify that 1 faraday corresponds to the charge required to deposit 1 mole of a substance based on its valence.
Determine that copper (Cu) has a valence of 2, meaning 1 mole of copper requires 2 faradays to deposit.
Calculate the moles of copper that can be deposited using 0.5 faradays: 0.5 faradays / 2 faradays per mole = 0.25 moles of copper.
Find the molar mass of copper, which is approximately 63.5 g/mol.
Multiply the moles of copper by its molar mass: 0.25 moles * 63.5 g/mol = 15.875 g, which rounds to 16 g.

text: How many structural isomers are there for a compound with the formula C<sub>7</sub>H<sub>16</sub>?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of compound based on the formula C7H16, which indicates it is an alkane.
Determine the possible carbon chain structures, including straight chains and branched chains.
Count all unique structural arrangements, ensuring that each isomer has a different connectivity of atoms.
Verify that no isomers are duplicates by checking for different branching and chain lengths.
Sum the total number of unique structural isomers found.

text: A particular reaction involves only one reactant, which decomposes into products. This reactant is also a strong absorber of yellow light, which allows a scientist to use a spectrometer to measure the reactant concentration as a function of time. The scientist then plots the natural logarithm of the reactant concentration as a function of time, and notices that the plot is linear. What is the order of the kinetics of this reaction?
explainAnswer: Identify that the reaction involves only one reactant decomposing into products.
Recognize that the plot of the natural logarithm of the concentration versus time being linear indicates first-order kinetics.
Recall that for first-order reactions, the rate of reaction is proportional to the concentration of the reactant.
Conclude that since the plot is linear, the reaction follows first-order kinetics.

text: A total of 50.0 milliliters of 0.100 molar sulfuric acid are used to titrate 10.0 milliliters of sodium hydroxide to its endpoint. Which of the following is the molarity of the sodium hydroxide?
explainAnswer: Calculate the number of moles of sulfuric acid using the formula: moles = molarity × volume (in liters).
Convert 50.0 milliliters of sulfuric acid to liters: 50.0 mL = 0.050 L.
Calculate moles of sulfuric acid: 0.100 mol/L × 0.050 L = 0.005 moles.
Determine the moles of sodium hydroxide needed using the balanced chemical equation: H2SO4 + 2 NaOH → Na2SO4 + 2 H2O, which shows 1 mole of H2SO4 reacts with 2 moles of NaOH.
Calculate moles of NaOH: 0.005 moles H2SO4 × 2 = 0.010 moles NaOH.
Convert the volume of sodium hydroxide from milliliters to liters: 10.0 mL = 0.010 L.
Finally, calculate the molarity of sodium hydroxide: molarity = moles/volume = 0.010 moles / 0.010 L = 1.00 M.

text: What do we call the ability of a single molecule to act both as a base and an acid?
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of acids and bases according to the Brønsted-Lowry theory.
Determine the characteristics of a substance that can donate protons (H+) and accept protons.
Look for a term that encompasses both behaviors of donating and accepting protons.
Conclude that the term describing this dual ability is 'amphoterism'.

text: By name or number, identify all of the following four characteristics that are intensive properties of a bubble of air: 1) density, 2) radius, 3) percent oxygen, 4) temperature.
explainAnswer: Understand that intensive properties do not depend on the amount of substance present.
Identify which of the characteristics listed can change with the size of the bubble.
Recognize that density, percent oxygen, and temperature remain constant regardless of the bubble's size.
Conclude that radius is an extensive property as it changes with the size of the bubble.

text: A plastic undergoes deformation at 740° Celsius. Given that its original cross-sectional area is 70 centimeters, its cross-sectional area after deformation is 62 centimeters, and its yield strength is 300 megapascals, determine the percent cold work to the nearest whole number.
explainAnswer: Calculate the change in cross-sectional area by subtracting the deformed area from the original area: 70 cm² - 62 cm² = 8 cm².
Determine the percent cold work using the formula: (change in area / original area) x 100%.
Substitute the values into the formula: (8 cm² / 70 cm²) x 100% = 11.43%.
Round the result to the nearest whole number to get the final percent cold work: 11%.

text: What is the name of the property that distinguishes L-alanine [AL-uh-neen] from D-alanine?
explainAnswer: Identify the structural differences between L-alanine and D-alanine.
Understand that chiral molecules have non-superimposable mirror images.
Recognize that the distinction between L and D forms is based on their spatial arrangement.
Conclude that the property distinguishing them is chirality.

text: Which of the following adjectives describes the reaction of a strong base with a strong acid?
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of the given adjectives: precipitation, synthesis, redox, and neutralization.
Recall that a strong base reacts with a strong acid to form water and a salt.
Recognize that this type of reaction is characterized as neutralization.
Eliminate the other choices based on their definitions and relevance to the reaction described.

text: Which of the following is true about the alpha particle?
choices: It was discovered by J.J. Thomson
It was used by Ernest Rutherford in experiments relating to the nucleus of the atom
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of an alpha particle, which consists of 2 protons and 2 neutrons.
Review historical context and experiments related to alpha particles, particularly those conducted by Ernest Rutherford.
Eliminate options that do not accurately describe the alpha particle, such as it being a hydrogen atom or purely electromagnetic radiation.
Confirm that the correct answer is related to Rutherford's experiments, which involved alpha particles and the structure of the atom.

text: What is the molecular formula for the conjugate base of the following Brønsted-Lowry acid: H<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>
explainAnswer: Identify the Brønsted-Lowry acid, which is H2CO3 (carbonic acid).
Determine what happens when this acid donates a proton (H+).
Remove one hydrogen atom from H2CO3 to form the conjugate base.
The resulting molecular formula after removing one H is HCO3.

text: Which of the following is one of the factors that determine the bonding between atoms in a solid?
choices: Magnitude of the electronegativities of the atoms
explainAnswer: Identify the factors that influence atomic bonding in solids.
Evaluate each choice based on its relevance to atomic bonding.
Recognize that electronegativity affects how atoms attract electrons.
Select the choice that directly relates to the bonding characteristics of atoms.

text: Bronze and brass are both alloys that are made by combining copper and another substance. What other substances are most typically used to make bronze and brass, respectively?
explainAnswer: Identify that bronze and brass are alloys primarily made from copper.
Recall that bronze is typically made by adding tin to copper.
Recognize that brass is usually created by combining zinc with copper.
Conclude that the other substances used are tin for bronze and zinc for brass.

text: Consisting of a fatty acid chain attached through an amide linkage to sphingosine [SFING-guh-seen], what is the fundamental structural unit common to all sphingolipids?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of sphingolipids, which include a fatty acid chain and sphingosine.
Understand that the amide linkage connects the fatty acid to sphingosine.
Recognize that the combination of these components forms a specific molecule.
Conclude that the fundamental structural unit formed is called ceramide.

text: Arrange the following 3 liquids in order of DECREASING surface tension at 20ºC: water; ethanol; mercury
explainAnswer: Identify the surface tension values of each liquid at 20ºC: Mercury has the highest surface tension, followed by water, and then ethanol.
Recall that surface tension is influenced by intermolecular forces; stronger forces lead to higher surface tension.
Recognize that mercury, being a metal, has very strong cohesive forces due to metallic bonding, resulting in the highest surface tension.
Understand that water has strong hydrogen bonding, which gives it a higher surface tension than ethanol, which has weaker hydrogen bonding.
Arrange the liquids in order from highest to lowest surface tension: Mercury, Water, Ethanol.

text: Transition metal elements have atoms or ions with which of the following orbitals partially filled?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of transition metals, which are found in the d-block of the periodic table.
Recall that transition metals are characterized by having partially filled d orbitals.
Eliminate the other options (f, p, s) based on their respective orbital characteristics and positions in the periodic table.
Conclude that the correct answer is d, as it represents the partially filled orbitals in transition metals.

text: Name all of the following five compounds that are soluble in water: 1) sodium sulfate, 2) lead (II) iodide, 3) barium chloride, 4) iron (II) hydroxide, 5) calcium sulfate.
explainAnswer: Identify the solubility rules for ionic compounds in water.
Check each compound against the solubility rules.
Sodium sulfate is soluble because all sodium salts are soluble.
Barium chloride is soluble because all chlorides of alkaline earth metals are soluble.
Lead (II) iodide, iron (II) hydroxide, and calcium sulfate are not soluble in water.

text: Which of the following is a weak electrolyte:
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of strong and weak electrolytes, noting that strong electrolytes completely dissociate in solution while weak electrolytes partially dissociate.
Evaluate each choice to determine their dissociation behavior in water.
Recognize that ammonia (NH3) is a weak base and does not fully dissociate in solution, making it a weak electrolyte.
Confirm that the other choices (dilute sulfuric acid, 1 molar sodium chloride, and dilute perchloric acid) are strong electrolytes as they fully dissociate in solution.

text: What separation technique would effectively separate a 50:50 mixture of ethanol and water?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of the mixture and their boiling points.
Recognize that ethanol has a lower boiling point than water.
Use fractional distillation to take advantage of the difference in boiling points.
Heat the mixture to vaporize the ethanol first.
Collect the vapor and condense it back into liquid ethanol, leaving water behind.

text: The PH<sub>3</sub> molecule has what type of molecular geometry?
explainAnswer: Identify the central atom in the PH3 molecule, which is phosphorus (P).
Count the number of bonding pairs and lone pairs of electrons around the central atom; phosphorus has three hydrogen atoms bonded and one lone pair.
Determine the molecular geometry based on the arrangement of bonding pairs and lone pairs; with three bonding pairs and one lone pair, the geometry is trigonal pyramidal.
Compare the identified geometry with the provided choices to confirm that 'Trigonal pyramidal' is the correct answer.

text: Put the following four compounds in order from least to most covalently bonded: 1) beryllium sulfide, 2) lithium oxide, 3) magnesium chloride, 4) calcium bromide.
explainAnswer: Identify the types of bonds in each compound: ionic or covalent.
Determine the electronegativity differences between the elements in each compound to assess bond character.
Rank the compounds based on the degree of covalent character, from least to most covalent.
List the compounds in the order based on their covalent character.

text: Which of the following molecules contains carbon-carbon bonds with the most s-character?
explainAnswer: Identify the hybridization of the carbon atoms in each molecule.
Determine the s-character of each hybridization: sp has 50% s-character, sp2 has 33% s-character, and sp3 has 25% s-character.
Compare the s-character percentages for ethane (sp3), ethene (sp2), ethyne (sp), and propane (sp3).
Conclude that ethyne has the highest s-character due to its sp hybridization.

text: To the second decimal place, what is the concentration of nitrate ions, in moles per liter, in a 0.26 molar Al(NO<sub>3</sub>)<sub>3</sub> solution?
explainAnswer: Identify the dissociation of Al(NO3)3 in solution, which produces 1 Al^3+ ion and 3 NO3^- ions.
Calculate the total number of moles of nitrate ions produced from 0.26 moles of Al(NO3)3, which is 3 times the moles of Al(NO3)3.
Multiply 0.26 moles by 3 to find the moles of nitrate ions: 0.26 * 3 = 0.78 moles.
Since the solution volume is 1 liter, the concentration of nitrate ions is 0.78 moles per liter.
Round the answer to the second decimal place, which remains 0.78.

text: You are given a particular polymer to study, and you notice that it can endure an extremely high amount of stress, but only a very small amount of strain. Which of the following types of polymer is it?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of the polymers listed in the choices.
Understand that a tough fiber is known for its ability to withstand high stress while exhibiting low strain.
Eliminate options that do not fit the description of high stress and low strain.
Confirm that tough fibers are specifically designed for strength and durability, making them the correct choice.

text: In which of the following ways would oxygen’s electrons fill the 3 p subshells?
explainAnswer: Identify the atomic number of oxygen, which is 8, indicating it has 8 electrons.
Determine the electron configuration of oxygen, which is 1s² 2s² 2p⁴.
Focus on the 2p subshell, which can hold a maximum of 6 electrons.
Distribute the 4 electrons in the 2p subshell: fill one orbital with a pair and place the remaining 2 electrons in separate orbitals, resulting in 1 pair and 2 unpaired electrons.

text: If you were to evaporate 1 liter or kilogram of water, how many calories of latent heat are stored in the vapor?
explainAnswer: Understand that the latent heat of vaporization for water is approximately 540 calories per gram.
Convert 1 liter of water to grams, knowing that 1 liter of water has a mass of 1000 grams.
Multiply the mass of the water (1000 grams) by the latent heat of vaporization (540 calories/gram).
Calculate 1000 grams × 540 calories/gram to find the total latent heat in calories.
The result is 540,000 calories, which can also be expressed as 5.4 × 10^5 calories.

text: Carbon dioxide has a boiling point of -57° Celsius, whereas sulfur dioxide has a boiling point of -10° Celsius. This difference is most likely due to the fact that sulfur dioxide exhibits which intermolecular force, while carbon dioxide does not?
explainAnswer: Identify the boiling points of carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide to understand their states at room temperature.
Recognize that the difference in boiling points indicates that sulfur dioxide has stronger intermolecular forces than carbon dioxide.
Recall that carbon dioxide is a nonpolar molecule, while sulfur dioxide is a polar molecule.
Determine that the presence of dipole-dipole interactions in sulfur dioxide contributes to its higher boiling point compared to carbon dioxide.

text: If the pK<sub>a</sub> of a weak acid is 4.74, what is the pK<sub>b</sub> of its conjugate base?
explainAnswer: Identify the relationship between pK<sub>a</sub> and pK<sub>b</sub> using the equation: pK<sub>a</sub> + pK<sub>b</sub> = 14.
Substitute the given pK<sub>a</sub> value into the equation: 4.74 + pK<sub>b</sub> = 14.
Rearrange the equation to solve for pK<sub>b</sub>: pK<sub>b</sub> = 14 - 4.74.
Calculate the value: pK<sub>b</sub> = 9.26.

text: What is the MOST common method for separating a mixture of liquids based on the differences in component volatilities?
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of the liquids in the mixture, particularly their boiling points.
Determine if the boiling points of the liquids are significantly different.
Apply the principle of distillation, which involves heating the mixture to vaporize the more volatile component.
Collect the vapor and condense it back into a liquid to separate it from the less volatile components.
Repeat the process if necessary to achieve a higher purity of the desired liquid.

text: Bottom-up approaches to nanotechnology generally involve microscopy. What technique is primarily involved in the top-down approach?
explainAnswer: Understand the difference between bottom-up and top-down approaches in nanotechnology.
Identify that bottom-up approaches build structures atom by atom or molecule by molecule.
Recognize that top-down approaches involve starting with larger materials and breaking them down.
Recall that lithography is a common technique used in the top-down approach to create patterns on surfaces.
Conclude that lithography is the primary technique associated with the top-down approach.

text: The release of hydrogen gas in the above experiment is called:
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the experiment involving hydrogen gas.
Determine the process that describes the release of gas bubbles in a liquid.
Eliminate options that do not fit the definition of gas release in this context.
Select the term that accurately describes the release of gas bubbles, which is 'effervescence'.

text: An airtight chamber contains 4 moles of nitrogen and an unknown amount of oxygen. If the partial pressure of oxygen is 150 torr, and the total pressure is 350 torr, how many moles of oxygen are present?
explainAnswer: Identify the total pressure and the partial pressure of oxygen.
Use the formula for total pressure: Total Pressure = Partial Pressure of Nitrogen + Partial Pressure of Oxygen.
Calculate the partial pressure of nitrogen by subtracting the partial pressure of oxygen from the total pressure.
Use the ideal gas law to find the number of moles of nitrogen and oxygen based on their partial pressures.
Solve for the number of moles of oxygen using the relationship between moles and partial pressures.

text: By name or number, identify all of the following four motions that describe how atoms in a methylene group can vibrate: 1) rocking, 2) symmetrical stretching, 3) see-sawing, 4) twisting.
answer: ROCKING, SYMMETRICAL STRETCHING, AND TWISTING (ACCEPT: 1, 2, AND
explainAnswer: Identify the types of molecular vibrations that can occur in a methylene group.
List the given options: rocking, symmetrical stretching, see-sawing, and twisting.
Determine which of the listed motions are valid vibrational modes for a methylene group.
Select the correct motions: rocking, symmetrical stretching, and twisting.

text: A solution is prepared by mixing 1 gram of ethanol with 100 grams of water to give a final volume of 101 milliliters. Calculate to the nearest integer the mass percent of ethanol in the solution.
explainAnswer: Determine the total mass of the solution by adding the mass of ethanol and the mass of water.
Calculate the mass percent of ethanol using the formula: (mass of ethanol / total mass of solution) * 100.
Substitute the values: (1 g / (1 g + 100 g)) * 100.
Simplify the calculation to find the mass percent of ethanol.
Round the result to the nearest integer.

text: Which of the following tends to crystallize in a simple cubic unit cell?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of crystal structures commonly associated with the given elements.
Recall that simple cubic unit cells are less common and typically found in specific elements.
Review the properties of each element listed to determine their crystallization patterns.
Confirm that Polonium is known to crystallize in a simple cubic structure, while the others do not.

text: Which of the following substances has the highest boiling point?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of intermolecular forces present in each substance.
Compare the strength of hydrogen bonding in water, methanol, and ethyl alcohol.
Note that diethyl ether has weaker dipole-dipole interactions and London dispersion forces.
Determine that water has the strongest hydrogen bonds, leading to the highest boiling point.

text: In preparing to perform a flame test on a sample, a high molar solution of which of the following chemicals would be best to use to clean your nichrome wire?
explainAnswer: Identify the purpose of cleaning the nichrome wire, which is to remove any contaminants that could affect the flame test results.
Evaluate the options provided for their ability to effectively clean metal surfaces.
